regressions: Tell the player the switch direction.
Allow the player to stop after turning.
successIndicators: Move the football without unnecessary delay.
matchApplication:
Switching play is used to:
Move away from defensive pressure.
Access the open side.
Change the angle of attack.
Exit defence.
Create uncontested possession.

title: Fake and Kick
objective: Develop the ability to use the eyes, shoulders and body position to move a defender before delivering the football to another target. Players learn to disguise their intended option without compromising kicking technique.
players: Minimum: 8 Ideal: 12–20 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
Place one central kicker with two receiving targets approximately 20–25 metres away, one left and one right.
Position one passive defender five to eight metres in front of the kicker.
A feeder stands behind the kicker with the football.
Players form lines at all positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder passes to the kicker.
The kicker scans both targets.
The kicker uses the eyes, shoulders or a short body movement to suggest one option.
The defender reacts towards the fake.
The kicker resets the body.
The kicker delivers to the opposite target.
Players rotate through each role.
Vary the direction of the fake.
The fake should be controlled and believable.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan both targets before the fake.
Use the eyes and shoulders to sell the first option.
Complete the kick with normal technique.
The fake is only valuable if it creates additional time or space.
progressions: Allow the defender to choose whether to react.
regressions: Use a coach as the defender.
Allow the kicker to begin with the football.
successIndicators: Move the defender with the fake.
matchApplication:
Fakes are used to:
Move a player on the mark.
Open a corridor kick.
Create a switch option.
Avoid a smother.
Disguise a forward entry.
Create time in congestion.

title: Switch Kick to Moving Target
primarySkill: Switching Play to a Moving Receiver
objective: Develop the ability to recognise a switch opportunity and deliver accurately to a teammate moving into open space on the opposite side of the ground. Players learn to scan early, open the body and weight the kick so the receiver can maintain momentum.
players: Minimum: 7 Ideal: 10–18 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
groundSize:
Medium to Large Area
Approximately 45 m × 35 m
setup:
Create three main positions:
Initial feeder.
Central receiver.
Switch receiver.
Place the feeder and central receiver approximately 15 metres apart.
Position the switch receiver’s starting cone 20–30 metres away on the opposite side and slightly forward of the central player.
Place a target cone another five to ten metres ahead of the switch receiver’s starting position.
Players form lines at each position.
howTheDrillWorks:
The central player scans towards the switch side.
The feeder kicks to the central player.
As the football travels, the switch receiver begins moving towards the target cone.
The central player marks the football.
The central player opens the body towards the switch.
The central player delivers the football into the receiver’s running path.
The switch receiver marks while continuing forward.
Players rotate through all positions.
Reverse the switching direction after several minutes.
The receiver should not stop and wait underneath the football.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan the switch side before receiving.
Mark with the body ready to open.
Identify the receiver’s speed and direction.
Kick to where the receiver is going.
The switch should move the football quickly into open space.
progressions: Add a player on the mark.
Allow the receiver to choose between two running lanes.
Require non-preferred foot use in one direction.
regressions: Tell the receiver when and where to move.
Allow the central player additional preparation time.
successIndicators: Allow the receiver to maintain momentum.
matchApplication:
This drill develops switching play during:
Defensive exits.
Half-back ball movement.
Wing transitions.
Changes of attacking angle.
Movement away from a congested side.

title: Long Switch Kick
objective: Develop the ability to execute a longer switch kick across the ground while maintaining accuracy and appropriate trajectory. Players learn to generate distance through controlled technique rather than sacrificing balance.
players: Minimum: 6 Ideal: 8–16 Maximum: 20 using multiple groups
setup:
Place one kicking position near one side of the ground.
Create a large receiving target zone 35–50 metres away on the opposite side.
Place a receiver inside the target zone.
A feeder stands approximately 10 metres from the kicker.
Players form lines at feeder, kicker and receiver positions.
Adjust distance according to age and kicking capability.
howTheDrillWorks:
The kicker scans the target zone.
The feeder passes to the kicker.
The kicker marks or gathers the football.
The kicker turns towards the opposite side.
The kicker uses a controlled approach.
The kicker delivers a long kick into the target zone.
The receiver marks or gathers.
Players rotate positions.
Practise switching in both directions.
Players score one point when the kick lands inside the target zone and two points when the receiver marks it.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Align the entire body with the target.
Generate power through leg speed and follow-through.
Use enough height to clear pressure without allowing excessive hang time.
Distance should increase only when accuracy remains acceptable.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Difference between preferred and non-preferred directions.
progressions: Add a player on the mark.
regressions: Allow the kicker to begin with the football.
successIndicators: Land kicks inside the target zone.
Give the receiver a realistic marking opportunity.
matchApplication:
Long switch kicks are used to:
Move the football away from defensive congestion.
Access the open side.
Change the angle of attack.
Exit defensive 50.
Transfer play across half-back.

title: Defensive Exit Switch
objective: Develop the ability to switch the football from a defensive position when the direct side is congested. Players learn to recognise pressure, use a safe release option and move the football towards the open side.
setup:
Create four positions:
Defensive ball carrier near one boundary.
Short central release target.
Opposite-side switch target.
Final outlet target further up the ground.
Place one passive defender near the direct-side option to represent congestion.
Players form lines at each attacking position.
howTheDrillWorks:
The defensive ball carrier begins with the football.
The defender positions to discourage the direct kick.
The ball carrier scans the central and opposite-side options.
The ball carrier kicks to the short central release target.
The central player marks and immediately opens towards the opposite side.
The central player kicks to the switch target.
The switch target marks and delivers to the final outlet.
Players follow their disposals and rotate.
Repeat from the opposite boundary.
The drill should move the football away from pressure rather than through it.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Recognise when the direct side is blocked.
Position the body to continue the switch.
Avoid holding the football long enough for pressure to recover.
The central release player is critical to the speed of the switch.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Initial decision by the defensive player.
Whether players force the direct option.
progressions: Allow defenders to adjust their positioning.
Add moving switch and outlet targets.
Continue into a live transition game.
successIndicators: Complete the switch before pressure recovers.
matchApplication:
This drill replicates defensive ball movement when:
One boundary is congested.
The opposition has shifted across.
A central release player is available.
The open side can be accessed.
A direct clearance would create a turnover risk.

title: Switch, Run and Receive
primarySkill: Following a Switch to Receive Again
objective: Develop the ability to switch the football and immediately support the next phase of play. Players learn that a kick does not end their involvement and practise running to receive again in a new position.
players: Minimum: 8 Ideal: 12–20 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
Create four positions in a wide diamond:
Starting player.
Central release.
Wide switch target.
Forward return target.
Place the starting player and central release approximately 15 metres apart.
Place the switch target 20–25 metres across the ground.
Place the return target 15–20 metres ahead of the switch target.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A kicks to the central release.
Player A immediately begins a hard support run across and forward.
The central release marks and kicks to the wide switch target.
The switch target marks and looks inside.
Player A continues the support run into the return lane.
The switch target kicks to Player A.
Player A marks and delivers to the forward target.
Players rotate through each position.
Repeat in both directions.
The original kicker must time the support run so they arrive after the switch has been completed.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Run with purpose rather than jogging.
Avoid arriving too early and becoming stationary.
The drill should demonstrate how a player can be involved multiple times in one possession chain.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the runner arrives in space.
progressions: Add a second possible returning runner.
Add a time target for completing the chain.
Finish with a shot at goal.
successIndicators: Maintain kicking quality under physical load.
matchApplication:
This drill develops repeat involvement during:
Defensive switches.
Half-back overlaps.
Wing transitions.
Give-and-go ball movement.
Attacking chains through the corridor.

title: Corridor Transfer Kick
primarySkill: Transferring the Football into the Corridor
objective: Develop the ability to move the football from a wide position into a central corridor target. Players learn to recognise when the central option is available and deliver a firm, accurate kick that supports continued forward movement.
players: Minimum: 8 Ideal: 12–20 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
Place one wide ball-carrier position near a boundary.
Create a corridor gate approximately four to six metres wide, 20–25 metres infield.
Position a central receiver beyond the gate.
Place a forward target another 20 metres ahead.
A passive defender begins near the corridor gate.
howTheDrillWorks:
The wide ball carrier receives from a feeder.
The central receiver presents through the corridor gate.
The defender moves to either partially close or leave the corridor lane.
The ball carrier scans the defender and central receiver.
When the lane is available, the ball carrier kicks firmly through the gate.
The central receiver marks and turns forward.
The central receiver kicks to the forward target.
Players rotate positions.
If the corridor is closed, the ball carrier uses a designated safe outlet before the drill resets.
The drill should reward correct recognition rather than forcing every kick into the corridor.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Recognise whether the corridor is open.
Avoid forcing the kick when pressure has closed the lane.
Prepare the central receiver to turn forward.
Maintain width when the corridor is unavailable.
Decision quality is as important as execution.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Scanning by the wide ball carrier.
Decision to use or avoid the corridor.
progressions: Use moving central and forward targets.
Continue into live play after the central mark.
regressions: Predetermine whether the lane is open.
successIndicators: Prepare the central receiver to continue forward.
matchApplication:
Corridor transfer kicks can:
Open the ground.
Create faster forward movement.
Move behind defensive pressure.
Improve scoring opportunities.
Change the point of attack.

title: Three-Kick Transition Chain
objective: Develop the ability to connect three consecutive kicks while moving the football from defence into attack. Players learn to prepare before receiving, maintain spacing and support the possession chain after disposal.
players: Minimum: 10 Ideal: 14–22 Maximum: 28 using multiple groups
setup:
Create four stations extending from defence towards attack:
Station A: Defensive start.
Station B: Short outlet.
Station C: Wide or central transition target.
Station D: Forward target.
Place each station 15–25 metres apart.
Players form lines at all stations.
Use a second football once the group understands the pattern.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A kicks to Player B.
Player A follows the disposal.
Player B scans, marks and turns towards Player C.
Player B kicks to Player C and follows.
Player C marks while moving or plays on immediately.
Player C kicks to Player D.
Player D marks and carries the football back along the outside of the drill.
All players rotate forward one station.
Continue for the allocated time.
Reverse the direction or change station angles.
The three kicks should vary in angle or distance rather than remain in a straight line.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan the next target before receiving.
Move the football quickly without rushing.
Adjust kicking weight for each distance.
Prepare the final target to attack the football.
The quality of the chain depends on every possession.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the second football creates congestion.
progressions: Introduce moving targets at every station.
Add a decision between two targets.
Require non-preferred foot use at one station.
Finish with a shot at goal.
regressions: Walk through the pattern before increasing pace.
successIndicators: Maintain accuracy under increasing physical load.
matchApplication:
This drill replicates transition ball movement through:
Defensive exit.
Half-back connection.
Wing or corridor movement.
Forward entry.
Repeated support running.

title: Boundary-to-Corridor Transition
primarySkill: Moving the Football from Boundary to Corridor
objective: Develop the ability to move possession from a wide boundary position into the corridor through a controlled sequence of kicks. Players learn to recognise the correct moment to transfer infield and continue the transition forward.
players: Minimum: 10 Ideal: 14–22 Maximum: 28 using multiple groups
setup:
Create four stations:
Boundary starting position.
Short boundary outlet.
Central corridor receiver.
Forward target.
Place the boundary outlet 15–20 metres ahead of the starting position.
Place the corridor receiver 20–25 metres infield from the boundary outlet.
Place the forward target another 20–30 metres ahead.
Position one passive defender between the boundary outlet and corridor receiver.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A begins with the football near the boundary.
Player A kicks to Player B at the short boundary outlet.
Player B scans the corridor before marking.
The passive defender adjusts position to either open or partially close the corridor.
If the corridor is open, Player B kicks to Player C infield.
Player C marks, turns forward and kicks to Player D.
If the corridor is closed, Player B uses a designated safe return option before the drill resets.
Players follow their disposals and rotate.
Repeat from both boundaries.
The drill should reward recognition rather than forcing the corridor kick every time.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Recognise whether the corridor is open.
Use a firm, accurate transfer kick.
Avoid floating the football into pressure.
Turn forward immediately after the central mark.
regressions: Predetermine when the corridor is open.
successIndicators: Continue forward after entering the corridor.
matchApplication:
This drill applies when teams:
Exit defence along the boundary.
Draw opponents towards one side.
Transfer into the corridor.
Create a more direct route to goal.
Change from safe possession to attacking transition.

title: Corridor-to-Forward Entry
objective: Develop the ability to deliver an effective forward entry after receiving possession in the corridor. Players learn to scan multiple forward options, recognise space and kick to the leading player’s advantage.
players: Minimum: 9 Ideal: 12–21 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
Place one corridor receiving position approximately 45–60 metres from goal or a designated scoring zone.
Create three forward starting positions:
Left lead.
Central lead.
Right lead.
Position one passive defender between the corridor player and the forwards.
A feeder stands 15 metres behind the corridor receiver.
howTheDrillWorks:
The corridor player scans all three forward positions.
The feeder kicks to the corridor player.
As the football travels, the forwards begin their leads.
The defender moves to influence one of the options.
The corridor player marks, assesses the available space and selects a target.
The corridor player kicks to the chosen forward’s advantage.
The forward marks or gathers and completes a shot at goal or target kick.
Players rotate through corridor, forward, defender and feeder roles.
Continue for the allocated time.
The forward entries should vary rather than follow a fixed sequence.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Use the lead that creates the greatest separation.
Place the football into the receiver’s path.
Use a lower trajectory when the lane is clear.
Make the decision before pressure arrives.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Timing and spacing of forward leads.
Whether forwards lead into the same space.
progressions: Allow forwards to choose their own leads.
matchApplication:
This drill replicates attacking possessions when players:
Win the football through the corridor.
Break a defensive line.
Deliver inside 50.
Select between several forward targets.
Need to avoid an intercept defender.

title: Inside-50 Target Selection
objective: Develop the ability to select the most effective target when entering the forward 50. Players learn to compare multiple options, recognise dangerous space and avoid kicking automatically to a crowded contest.
players: Minimum: 10 Ideal: 14–22 Maximum: 28 using multiple groups
setup:
Create one ball-carrier position outside forward 50.
Set three forward options:
Short lead.
Deep lead.
Lateral lead into space.
Position two passive defenders to influence the available options.
A feeder stands behind the ball carrier.
Players form lines at all positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier scans the forward structure.
The feeder delivers the football.
As the ball carrier receives, the three forwards begin different leads.
The defenders adjust to cover or influence selected options.
The ball carrier chooses the target that offers:
The greatest separation.
The safest kicking lane.
The strongest scoring opportunity.
The ball carrier delivers the football.
The selected forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
Players rotate through all roles.
Continue for the allocated time.
The coach may award points for decision quality, kick execution and scoring outcome.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Use short leads when deep space is unavailable.
Use an appropriate kick type and trajectory.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players repeatedly choose the deepest option.
Whether decisions create realistic shots at goal.
progressions: Continue into live play after the entry.
matchApplication:
This drill develops decision making during one of the most important moments in Australian Football: the kick inside 50.
It applies to:
Fast entries.
Slow possession entries.
Entries from the corridor.
Entries from the boundary.
Rebound and turnover situations.

title: Forward Entry to Space
objective: Develop the ability to kick into open forward space so a teammate can attack the football at speed. Players learn to place the ball away from defenders and avoid kicking directly to a stationary target.
players: Minimum: 8 Ideal: 12–20 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
Place one ball-carrier position 40–55 metres from goal or a target area.
Create three forward-entry zones:
Left pocket space.
Central space.
Right pocket space.
A forward begins behind the zones.
A passive defender begins between the forward and ball carrier.
A feeder stands behind the ball carrier.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier receives from the feeder.
The forward observes the defender’s position.
The forward leads towards the open target zone.
The ball carrier reads the lead.
The ball carrier kicks into the selected space.
The forward attacks the football at speed.
The forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
Players rotate roles.
Continue from different entry angles.
The football should be placed into space rather than directly onto the forward’s head unless the lead demands it.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Use space in front of the forward.
Match kicking weight to the lead.
Keep the ball low enough to reduce defensive recovery time.
Allow the forward to maintain speed.
Recognise when space is more valuable than a direct pass.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the football remains inside the target area.
progressions: Allow the forward to choose any zone.
successIndicators: Allow the forward to maintain speed.
matchApplication:
Kicking to forward space is especially valuable when:
The forward line is open.
Defenders are positioned goal side.
A teammate has speed advantage.
Direct marking targets are unavailable.
The team is attacking from turnover.

title: Lowered-Eyes Forward Entry
objective: Develop the habit of lowering the eyes before entering forward 50 and identifying short or lateral targets rather than automatically kicking long to a contest.
players: Minimum: 9 Ideal: 12–21 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
Place the ball carrier outside forward 50.
Create:
One deep forward target.
Two short lead targets.
One lateral target.
Position one or two passive defenders near the deep option.
A feeder stands 15 metres behind the ball carrier.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier scans the forward line before receiving.
The feeder passes to the ball carrier.
The deep forward and short targets begin their movements.
The defenders influence the deep option.
The ball carrier lowers the eyes and assesses the shorter targets.
The ball carrier selects the best available option.
The receiver marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
Players rotate through all roles.
Continue with different defensive positions.
The deep option remains available when it is genuinely the best choice.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Avoid becoming fixed on the goal square.
Place the football in front of the receiver.
Remain patient while moving at speed.
Understand that a shorter kick may create a better shot.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the player scans short options.
Whether the player defaults to the deep kick.
Quality of the resulting scoring chance.
progressions: Add a closing defender behind the ball carrier.
Allow defenders to cover short options.
regressions: Use one short and one deep target.
matchApplication:
Lowered-eyes entries are important when:
Defenders drop deep.
The goal square is crowded.
Short forwards create separation.
A lateral option improves the scoring angle.
Controlled possession is preferable to a contest.

title: Deep versus Short Entry Decision
primarySkill: Choosing Between Deep and Short Forward Entries
objective: Develop the ability to compare a deep attacking option with a shorter possession option and select the entry that creates the strongest scoring opportunity.
players: Minimum: 9 Ideal: 12–21 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
Create:
One ball-carrier position outside forward 50.
One deep forward starting near goal.
One short forward starting 25–35 metres from goal.
One defender assigned to influence the deep option.
One second defender positioned between the short and deep areas.
A feeder stands behind the ball carrier.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier scans both forward options.
The feeder passes to the ball carrier.
The deep and short forwards begin their leads.
The defenders adjust their positioning.
The ball carrier assesses:
Separation.
Defender numbers.
Kicking lane.
Likely scoring outcome.
The ball carrier selects either the deep or short option.
The receiver marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
Players rotate through all roles.
Continue with varied defensive positioning.
The coach should avoid making one option permanently preferable.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Compare the quality of both options.
Use the deep target when separation is clear.
Use the short option when defenders protect space behind.
Make the decision early enough to reward the lead.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the player repeatedly chooses one option.
Quality of the resulting shot at goal.
matchApplication:
This drill develops forward-entry decisions when:
A deep forward has separation.
Defenders drop behind the ball.
A short lead presents inside 50.
The ball carrier must choose between territory and possession.
The quality of the next shot matters more than distance gained.

title: Forward Entry Under Chasing Pressure
objective: Develop the ability to deliver an effective forward entry while a defender applies pressure from behind. Players learn to accelerate into space, scan the forward line early and complete the kick before pressure forces a rushed disposal.
players: Minimum: 10 Ideal: 14–22 Maximum: 28 using multiple groups
setup:
Place:
One ball-carrier starting cone 55–65 metres from goal.
One chasing defender’s cone three to five metres behind.
Three forward starting positions inside 50.
Optional left, central and right target zones.
The ball carrier begins with the football.
The forwards begin in separate leading lanes.
howTheDrillWorks:
On the coach’s signal, the ball carrier and chasing defender begin.
The ball carrier accelerates towards forward 50.
The forwards begin their leads.
The ball carrier scans the available targets while running.
The defender closes from behind without tackling.
The ball carrier selects the best option and delivers before the defender reaches effective pressure.
The selected forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
Players rotate through ball-carrier, defender and forward roles.
Adjust the defender’s starting gap to suit the group.
The ball carrier should not wait until reaching the 50-metre line if a strong option appears earlier.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Prepare the football before the defender closes.
Recognise the first strong forward option.
Maintain balance through the final steps.
The player should remain composed and use the space created by their acceleration.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the defender maintains safe pressure.
Adjust the starting gap if the defender consistently reaches the kicker too early.
progressions: Allow controlled tackling before the kicking line.
successIndicators: Prepare the football before pressure arrives.
matchApplication:
This drill applies when players:
Break from congestion.
Receive an overlap handball.
Attack from turnover.
Carry through the corridor.
Enter forward 50 under recovery pressure.

title: Forward Entry with Closing Defender
objective: Develop the ability to create and use a forward-entry kicking lane while a defender closes from the front. Players learn to recognise the defender’s line, make a small angle change and deliver into the forward 50 without kicking into smothering pressure.
players: Minimum: 10 Ideal: 14–22 Maximum: 28 using multiple groups
setup:
Place:
One ball-carrier position outside forward 50.
One closing defender 10–12 metres ahead.
Two forward-entry gates, one left and one right of the defender.
One forward target beyond each gate.
One feeder behind the ball carrier.
Players form lines at all positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder passes to the ball carrier.
The defender closes from the front with hands raised.
The forwards begin leads through the two entry gates.
The ball carrier scans the defender and forward options.
The ball carrier moves slightly off the defender’s line.
The ball carrier delivers through the clearer gate.
The selected forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
Players rotate through all roles.
Vary defender closing angles.
The defender pressures the lane without making unsafe contact.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan both entry lanes before receiving.
Select the forward away from pressure.
Maintain a compact and balanced kick.
Release before the defender reaches smothering distance.
matchApplication:
This drill applies when players:
Exit a stoppage towards forward 50.
Receive in the corridor.
Approach a high defender.
Enter forward 50 under frontal pressure.
Need to avoid an intercept or smother.

title: Forward Entry After Evasion
primarySkill: Forward Entry After Beating an Opponent
objective: Develop the ability to evade an opponent before delivering accurately inside 50. Players learn to use the evasive movement to create time and a better kicking angle rather than rushing immediately after beating the defender.
players: Minimum: 10 Ideal: 14–22 Maximum: 28 using multiple groups
setup:
Place:
One attacker’s starting cone outside forward 50.
One evasion defender eight metres ahead.
Two exit gates around the defender.
Three forward leading lanes beyond the exit gates.
One feeder behind the attacker.
Players form lines at all positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder passes to the attacker.
The attacker moves towards the evasion defender.
The defender shades one side.
The attacker uses a sidestep, baulk or change of pace to exit through the opposite gate.
The forwards begin their leads.
The attacker accelerates out of the evasion.
The attacker scans and delivers to the best available forward.
The selected forward finishes at goal.
Players rotate through all roles.
Vary the defender’s positioning and forward leads.
The attacker should not kick while still moving sharply sideways.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Protect the football during the evasion.
Lift the eyes immediately after escaping.
Use the space created to execute cleanly.
The evasion should improve the forward entry rather than delay it unnecessarily.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the player rushes after evading.
progressions: Reduce the size of exit gates.
regressions: Replace the defender with a pole.
Allow the attacker to stop after evading.
matchApplication:
This drill applies when players:
Beat a midfielder at the top of forward 50.
Step around a high defender.
Escape congestion.
Create a better forward-entry angle.
Turn a pressured possession into an attacking opportunity.

title: Forward Entry After Ground Ball
primarySkill: Forward Entry After a Ground Ball Gather
objective: Develop the ability to gather a loose football outside forward 50 and quickly convert possession into an effective forward entry. Players learn to secure the football first, accelerate from the contest and identify the best attacking option.
players: Minimum: 9 Ideal: 12–21 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
Place:
One starting cone 55 metres from goal.
One ground-ball collection zone eight metres ahead.
Three forward starting positions inside 50.
One feeder beside the collection zone.
Players form lines at the starting and forward positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker runs towards the collection zone.
The feeder rolls the football into the attacker’s path.
The attacker gathers cleanly.
The attacker accelerates away from the collection point.
The forwards begin their leads.
The attacker scans and selects the best option.
The attacker delivers inside 50.
The forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
Players rotate through all positions.
Vary the ground-ball angle and forward leads.
The player should not look forward before securing possession.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Get low and use two hands.
Take the first steps away from the collection point.
Lift the eyes early after the gather.
Prepare the football during the run.
Select the forward with the best space.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the player rushes immediately after gathering.
regressions: Allow the player to stop after gathering.
matchApplication:
This drill applies when players:
Win a loose ball outside forward 50.
Gather a spill from a contest.
Recover a turnover.
Crumb a marking contest.
Attack before the opposition can reset.

title: Forward Entry After Handball Receive
primarySkill: Forward Entry After an Overlap Handball
objective: Develop the ability to receive a handball at speed outside forward 50 and deliver accurately to a leading forward. Players learn to time the support run, receive in front and prepare the football without losing momentum.
players: Minimum: 10 Ideal: 14–22 Maximum: 28 using multiple groups
setup:
Create:
One initial ball carrier outside forward 50.
One support runner starting behind and to the side.
Three forward leading positions.
One feeder or starting line.
The initial ball carrier begins with the football.
The support runner starts three to five metres behind.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier begins moving towards forward 50.
The support runner delays, then accelerates past.
The support runner calls for the football.
The ball carrier handballs into the runner’s path.
The forwards begin their leads.
The support runner receives without slowing.
The support runner scans and delivers to the best forward option.
The selected forward finishes at goal.
Players rotate through all roles.
Repeat from both sides.
The handball should release the runner into space rather than towards pressure.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Receive in front of the body.
Scan the forward line before and during the receive.
progressions: Allow the ball carrier to choose whether to handball.
regressions: Allow the receiver to stop before kicking.
matchApplication:
This drill applies when players:
Create an overlap through the middle.
Receive a release handball.
Break the defensive line.
Enter forward 50 at speed.
Deliver before defenders can recover.

title: Forward Entry from Boundary
primarySkill: Forward Entry from a Wide Angle
objective: Develop the ability to enter forward 50 effectively from near the boundary. Players learn to assess central, short and deep options while avoiding predictable kicks directly down the line.
players: Minimum: 10 Ideal: 14–22 Maximum: 28 using multiple groups
setup:
Place one ball-carrier position near the boundary outside forward 50.
Create three forward targets:
Short lead along the boundary.
Central lead into the corridor side of forward 50.
Deep lead towards goal.
Position one passive defender to influence the central lane and another near the deep option.
A feeder stands behind the ball carrier.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier scans all forward targets.
The feeder delivers the football.
The forwards begin their leads.
The defenders adjust their positioning.
The ball carrier selects the best available entry.
The ball carrier delivers to the receiver’s advantage.
The selected forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
Players rotate through all roles.
Repeat from both boundaries.
The central option should be used when available, but not forced.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan inside before defaulting down the line.
Open the hips towards central targets.
Use the short option if deep space is crowded.
Adjust trajectory for the selected lead.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Quality of the resulting scoring chance.
progressions: Add a player on the mark.
regressions: Allow the player to begin stationary with the football.
successIndicators: Scan inside and down the line.
matchApplication:
This drill applies when players:
Enter forward 50 from the wing.
Possess near the boundary.
Need to avoid a crowded deep contest.
Access a central forward.
Use a short lead to improve the scoring angle.

title: Forward Entry from Opposite Foot
objective: Develop the ability to deliver inside 50 using the non-preferred foot when body position, pressure or field location removes the preferred-side option.
players: Minimum: 8 Ideal: 12–20 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
Place one ball-carrier position outside forward 50.
Create two leading targets positioned so the non-preferred foot provides the more natural kicking angle.
A feeder stands 10–15 metres behind or beside the ball carrier.
Players rotate through feeder, kicker and forward roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The kicker receives from the feeder.
The forwards begin their leads.
The kicker must use the non-preferred foot.
The kicker selects the better of the two targets.
The kicker delivers to the receiver’s advantage.
The selected forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
Players rotate positions.
Repeat from both sides of the ground.
Keep the distance realistic enough for sound technique.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Hold the football correctly for the non-preferred side.
Guide it directly over the kicking foot.
Select a target within realistic range.
Avoid turning back onto the preferred foot automatically.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Willingness to use the non-preferred foot.
Whether players turn back into pressure.
progressions: Add passive pressure on the preferred side.
regressions: Return to basic non-preferred foot kicking.
matchApplication:
Non-preferred foot forward entries are required when:
Opponents block the preferred side.
Players receive near the boundary.
Body position limits turning.
Fast ball movement demands immediate disposal.
A teammate is open on the opposite angle.

title: Forward Entry Decision Game
objective: Develop live forward-entry decisions in a constrained game. Players learn to select between leading targets, space, short possession and deeper options while defenders actively influence the available lanes.
players: Minimum: 12 Ideal: 16–24 Maximum: 30 using two areas
setup:
Create a playing area extending from approximately 70 metres from goal to the goal line.
Divide players into:
Attacking team.
Defending team.
Optional neutral transition players.
Recommended starting format:
Four to six attackers.
Three to five defenders.
One or two neutral players outside forward 50.
Start each repetition with a neutral player or coach feeding the football to an attacker outside 50.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team gains possession outside forward 50.
Forwards create leads and maintain spacing.
Defenders attempt to deny the most dangerous options.
The ball carrier decides whether to:
Kick to a leading forward.
Kick into space.
Use a short possession.
Switch the angle.
Retain the football.
The attack continues until:
A shot at goal is completed.
The defence wins possession.
The football leaves the area.
Reset and begin a new repetition.
Rotate attackers and defenders regularly.
Award points for decision quality as well as scoring.
Optional scoring:
Three points for a marked kick that creates a shot.
Two points for a forward gathering a kick to advantage.
One point for retaining possession inside 50.
Bonus point for using a non-preferred foot successfully.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Avoid leading into the same area.
Avoid low-percentage kicks to outnumbered contests.
Retain possession when no strong entry exists.
The coach should avoid stopping every repetition. Allow players to experience the consequences of their decisions.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players retain possession when required.
Use brief feedback between repetitions rather than constant interruption.
progressions: Add transition after a defensive turnover.
Restrict the number of possessions before entry.
Track entry type and scoring outcome.
regressions: Stop after the first forward entry.
matchApplication:
This drill directly replicates live inside-50 decision making, including:
Fast entries.
Slow entries.
Boundary entries.
Corridor entries.
Kicks to space.
Short possession.
Deep contests.
Entries under pressure.

title: Short Kick Retention
objective: Develop the ability to retain possession using short, accurate kicks. Players learn to control the weight and trajectory of the football so the receiver can mark cleanly and continue the possession chain.
players: Minimum: 6 Ideal: 9–18 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
groundSize:
Small to Medium Area
Approximately 30 m × 25 m
setup:
Create four stations in a square or diamond.
Recommended spacing:
Under 10–12: 10–12 metres.
Under 14 and above: 15–20 metres.
Place two to four players at each station.
Begin with one football.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A kicks to Player B at the next station.
Player B marks the football.
Player A follows the kick to the back of Player B’s line.
Player B turns and kicks to Player C.
The pattern continues around the area.
Change direction after several minutes.
Add a second football once players maintain accuracy and spacing.
Every kick should travel a realistic short-marking distance for the age group.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Kick to the receiver’s chest or advantage.
Control the power of the kick.
Avoid kicking too hard at short range.
Prepare the next target before receiving.
progressions: Add a passive defender in the centre.
Introduce a time target for completing a circuit.
regressions: Allow players to handball through the pattern first.
successIndicators: Retain possession through the full circuit.
matchApplication:
Short kicks are used to:
Retain possession.
Move around defensive zones.
Exit defence safely.
Control tempo.
Find uncontested teammates.
Improve the angle of the next disposal.

title: Short Kick and Reposition
objective: Develop the ability to complete a short kick and immediately reposition to support the next possession. Players learn to create a new passing option instead of remaining where the original disposal was made.
players: Minimum: 6 Ideal: 9–18 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
Create three main passing stations in a triangle.
Place one support cone approximately five to eight metres away from each passing station.
Players form lines at the three main stations.
The football begins at one station.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A kicks to Player B.
Player A immediately runs to the nearby support cone.
Player B marks and turns towards Player C.
Player B kicks to Player C.
Player B runs to their support cone.
Player C may kick to the repositioned Player A rather than continuing directly around the triangle.
Players continue moving between main and support positions.
Rotate the direction after several minutes.
The drill should create repeated short options rather than a fixed circular pattern.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Avoid running behind the player with the football.
Avoid standing on the same line as another target.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players become hidden behind others.
Whether players stop once reaching a cone.
progressions: Convert into a live keepings-off game.
regressions: Pause and reset after every three kicks.
matchApplication:
Players must reposition after kicking to:
Create a return option.
Support a switch.
Provide an outlet.
Maintain possession.
Prevent the ball carrier becoming isolated.

title: Possession Triangle
objective: Develop the ability to retain possession through short angled kicks. Players learn to create passing lanes, receive side-on and move the football away from pressure.
groundSize:
Small to Medium Area
Approximately 25 m × 25 m
setup:
Place three cones in a triangle.
Position one support cone between each main cone and slightly inside the triangle.
Players form lines at the three outside cones.
The football begins at one outside cone.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A kicks to Player B at the next outside cone.
Player A moves to the nearby support cone.
Player B scans before marking.
Player B may kick:
Directly to Player C.
Back to Player A at the support cone.
The receiving player continues the possession.
All players move after disposal.
Change direction after several minutes.
The coach may initially nominate the option before allowing players to decide.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan both direct and support options.
Avoid standing behind a defender or teammate.
Use the safer option when the direct lane is closed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players force the direct kick.
regressions: Allow players to walk through the pattern.
matchApplication:
Triangular support structures help teams:
Retain possession.
Move around defenders.
Create safer kicking angles.
Switch play.
Support the ball carrier.

title: Short Kick Keepings-Off
objective: Develop the ability to retain possession using short kicks while a defender pressures the available passing lanes. Players learn to move into space, select safe options and avoid predictable disposals.
setup:
Create a rectangular playing area.
Recommended formats:
Four attackers versus one defender.
Five attackers versus two defenders.
Attackers spread around the outside and inside of the area.
Defenders begin centrally.
howTheDrillWorks:
Attackers retain possession using kicks only.
The player with the football may not run more than several steps.
Defenders attempt to intercept or spoil.
After a mark, the receiver has a limited time to dispose.
Attackers score one point for every five completed kicks.
If defenders win possession, rotate the player responsible for the turnover into defence.
Continue for timed blocks.
The coach may allow handball as a regression.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
progressions: Remove stationary marks and require continuous play.
matchApplication:
This drill develops possession control when teams need to:
Slow the game.
Maintain the football.
Move around a defensive zone.
protect a lead.
Create a better attacking angle.

title: Three-versus-One Kicking Possession
objective: Develop the ability to use a three-versus-one advantage to retain possession and move the football past a defender. Players learn to maintain width, draw pressure and release to the free target.
players: Minimum: 4 Ideal: 8–16 using multiple groups Maximum: 20
groundSize:
Small Area
Approximately 20 m × 15 m per group
setup:
Create a rectangular area.
Place three attackers around the outside edges.
Position one defender inside the area.
One attacker begins with the football.
howTheDrillWorks:
The three attackers retain possession using kicks.
The defender pressures the ball carrier and attempts to intercept.
Attackers may move along the boundaries or into open space.
The ball carrier scans both teammates.
The ball carrier draws the defender before releasing to the free player.
Attackers score one point for every three consecutive marks.
Rotate the defender after a turnover or set period.
Continue for multiple rounds.
Kicking distances must remain legal and appropriate for the group.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Draw the defender without holding too long.
Kick to the free player’s advantage.
Avoid standing in the same lane.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether attackers stand in one line.
Whether the same player dominates possession.
progressions: Require attackers to progress towards an end zone.
regressions: Use a coach as the defender.
matchApplication:
Three-versus-one situations occur during:
Defensive rebound.
Overlap play.
Switches.
Loose-ball wins.
Attacking transition.

title: Possession Kick with End Zones
objective: Develop the ability to retain possession while progressing the football towards an end zone. Players learn to balance safe passing with forward movement and recognise when to retain, switch or attack.
setup:
Create a rectangular playing area with an end zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
Recommended format:
Five versus five.
Six versus six.
Optional neutral players along the outside.
Each team attacks a nominated end zone.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins play with one team in possession.
Teams move the football using kicks.
A team scores by completing a marked kick to a teammate inside the attacking end zone.
Players may not remain permanently inside an end zone.
After a score, possession begins with the opposing team.
If the football is intercepted or leaves the area, possession changes.
Play for timed blocks.
Rotate the attacking direction.
Optional rules:
A minimum of three kicks before scoring.
No consecutive kicks to the same player.
Bonus points for switching sides before scoring.
Bonus points for a non-preferred foot kick.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Use short possession to move defenders.
Recognise when the end zone becomes available.
coachingCues: “Attack the end zone at the right time.”
progressions: Add a second football for separate groups.
Transition into a larger conditioned game.
matchApplication:
This drill develops the balance between possession and territory during:
Defensive exits.
Controlled transitions.
Late-game possession.
Movement through zones.
Attacking entries against an organised defence.

title: Four-versus-Two Kicking Grid
objective: Develop the ability to retain possession in a four-versus-two numerical advantage. Players learn to create width, provide multiple kicking options and move the football before the defenders can close the available lanes.
players: Minimum: 6 Ideal: 12–18 using multiple groups Maximum: 24
groundSize:
Small to Medium Area
Approximately 25 m × 20 m per group
setup:
Create a rectangular grid.
Place four attackers around the outside and inside edges of the grid.
Position two defenders centrally.
One attacker begins with the football.
Recommended starting dimensions:
Under 12–14: 25 m × 20 m.
Under 16 and above: 22 m × 18 m.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attackers retain possession using kicks.
The defenders attempt to intercept, spoil or force an error.
The ball carrier may move a limited number of steps.
Attackers score one point for every four completed marks.
If the defenders win possession or force the football out, the player responsible for the turnover rotates into defence.
The longest-serving defender rotates out.
Continue for timed blocks.
Restart quickly after every turnover.
Optional rule:
At least one attacker must occupy the inside of the grid rather than all four remaining on the boundary.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Create at least two visible options.
The numerical advantage should allow possession, but only if players maintain good spacing.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether all players crowd the boundary.
progressions: Remove the mark and continue play from any clean possession.
matchApplication:
This drill develops possession under moderate pressure during:
Defensive exits.
Half-back control.
Switching play.
Numerical advantages.
Late-game possession.
Movement around a zone.

title: Kicking Possession Transition Game
objective: Develop the ability to retain possession through kicking and transition immediately when possession changes. Players learn to spread quickly in attack, close space in defence and make effective decisions during turnover moments.
setup:
Create a rectangular playing area.
Divide players into two teams.
Recommended formats:
Five versus five with two neutral players.
Six versus six.
Seven versus seven in a larger area.
Neutral players, if used, always play with the team in possession.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins play with one team.
The team in possession retains the football using kicks.
One point is awarded for every five consecutive marks.
If possession changes, the new attacking team spreads immediately.
The team that lost possession transitions into defence.
Play continues without stopping after interceptions or loose-ball wins.
Restart only when the football leaves the area or becomes trapped.
Play for timed blocks.
Optional scoring:
Two points for five consecutive kicks followed by a successful switch.
Bonus point for a non-preferred foot kick.
Bonus point for winning the football back within five seconds of a turnover.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Close space immediately after losing possession.
Recognise when to play quickly and when to retain.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Decision making immediately after possession changes.
Whether players switch mentally between attack and defence.
progressions: Add a second phase after a completed possession target.
matchApplication:
Turnovers are among the most important moments in Australian Football.
This drill develops the ability to:
Attack before the opposition resets.
Defend before the opposition spreads.
Retain possession after winning the ball.
Avoid immediate turnover chains.
Use kicking skills under changing conditions.

title: Zone-to-Zone Kicking Game
primarySkill: Progressing the Football Through Field Zones
objective: Develop the ability to progress possession through multiple field zones using controlled kicks. Players learn to create options ahead of the football, maintain support behind it and recognise when to retain or advance.
setup:
Divide a rectangular playing area into three horizontal zones:
Defensive zone.
Midfield zone.
Attacking zone.
Divide players into two teams.
Optional neutral players may operate in the midfield zone.
Each team attacks a nominated end.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins in one team’s defensive zone.
The team must progress the football through the midfield zone before entering the attacking zone.
Players may move between zones, but the coach may initially restrict numbers in each zone.
A point is scored when a player marks a kick inside the attacking end zone.
If possession changes, the new team attacks in the opposite direction.
Play continues through turnovers.
Restart after scores or when the football leaves the area.
Play for timed blocks.
Optional conditions:
At least one kick must be completed in each zone.
A switch must occur before entering the attacking zone.
Players may not kick over an entire zone.
Bonus points for a corridor transition.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Create options ahead and behind the football.
Recognise when the next zone is available.
Retain possession when forward lanes are closed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players bypass the intended learning outcome.
progressions: Finish with a shot at goal.
regressions: Stop play after each successful zone entry.
matchApplication:
This drill develops team kicking patterns across:
Defensive exit.
Midfield transition.
Forward entry.
Switches.
Corridor movement.
Controlled possession.

title: Turnover Kick Challenge
objective: Develop the quality of the first kick after possession changes. Players learn to recognise whether to attack immediately, retain possession or move the football away from pressure following a turnover.
groundSize:
Medium to Large Area
Approximately 55 m × 40 m
setup:
Create a rectangular playing area with one scoring target at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
The coach begins each repetition by creating a turnover through:
A loose-ball feed.
An intentionally intercepted pass.
A contested possession.
A coach’s call changing the attacking team.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team gains possession after the turnover.
The player winning the football must quickly assess:
Immediate forward option.
Safe lateral option.
Support behind the football.
The first kick is completed.
Play continues towards the attacking target.
The team scores by completing a marked kick in the end zone or kicking a goal.
If possession changes again, play continues in the opposite direction.
Reset after a score or the football leaves the area.
Play for timed blocks.
The coach may award two points when the first kick after turnover leads directly to a scoring chain.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Recognise whether the opposition is organised.
Attack quickly when space is available.
Retain possession when the first forward option is unsafe.
Use the first kick to establish team control.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players kick automatically without assessing.
Outcome of the first possession chain.
progressions: Require non-preferred foot use in selected scenarios.
regressions: Stop after the first kick for coaching.
matchApplication:
The first kick after turnover can determine whether a team:
Launches a fast attack.
Retains possession.
Re-enters congestion.
Gives the football back.
Creates a scoring opportunity.

title: Defensive-to-Attacking Transition Kick
primarySkill: Transition Kicking from Defence to Attack
objective: Develop the ability to move the football from a defensive possession into attack through a coordinated kicking chain. Players learn to spread quickly, identify the most dangerous available lane and support the football through multiple phases.
setup:
Create:
A defensive starting zone.
A midfield transition zone.
A forward scoring zone.
Place one defensive player with the football or begin from an intercept feed.
Position attacking teammates across half-back, wing, corridor and forward positions.
Add passive defenders who recover as the ball moves.
howTheDrillWorks:
The defensive player gains possession.
Attacking teammates spread immediately.
The defensive player selects the first outlet kick.
The receiving player scans and continues the transition through either:
The corridor.
A wide switch.
An overlap support option.
Defenders recover and attempt to close the available lanes.
The attacking team completes a forward entry and shot at goal.
If defenders win possession, they transition in the opposite direction.
Reset after a score or turnover outside the area.
Rotate starting positions.
The coach should vary the initial defensive location.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Spread immediately after possession is won.
Use the first safe kick to establish control.
Attack quickly if the opposition is unbalanced.
Switch if the direct side is closed.
Support behind and ahead of the football.
Maintain kicking quality under physical load.
progressions: Require alternating corridor and wide transitions.
regressions: Stop after each kick for coaching.
matchApplication:
This drill replicates full-field movement after:
An intercept mark.
A defensive ground-ball win.
A turnover at half-back.
A kick-in possession.
A defensive stoppage clearance.

title: Intercept Mark Transition Kick
objective: Develop the ability to take an intercept mark, scan immediately and launch an effective transition kick before the opposition can recover defensively.
players: Minimum: 9 Ideal: 12–21 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
Create:
One attacking feeder outside a defensive zone.
One intended attacking target.
One intercept defender positioned between them.
Three transition targets:
Short outlet.
Wide switch.
Central attacking option.
Players form lines at all positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder kicks towards the intended attacking target.
The intercept defender reads the kick and moves to mark.
As the intercept occurs, the three transition targets move into their lanes.
The intercept player scans immediately.
The intercept player selects and completes the best transition kick.
The receiver marks and continues the possession to a final target.
Players rotate through feeder, attacker, interceptor and transition roles.
Vary the location and height of the initial kick.
The intercept player may play on or use a controlled kick from the mark.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Mark at the highest safe point.
Use the first strong transition option.
Avoid automatically kicking down the line.
Maintain accuracy after the intercept effort.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Scanning before and after the mark.
Whether the player defaults to a predictable option.
progressions: Increase the difficulty of the intercept.
Allow a live attacker to pressure after the mark.
Continue into a full transition game.
regressions: Allow the interceptor to stop before disposal.
successIndicators: Move the football before defensive recovery.
matchApplication:
Intercept marks create strong attacking opportunities because the opposition is often positioned for attack rather than defence.
This drill develops the ability to convert an intercept into:
A fast switch.
A corridor transition.
A safe short outlet.
A forward attack.
A repeat possession chain.

title: Intercept and Switch
objective: Develop the ability to recognise and execute a switch immediately after winning an intercept possession. Players learn to use the opposition’s movement towards one side to access space on the opposite side.
setup:
Place:
One feeder on a boundary side.
One intended attacking target.
One intercept player between them.
One short release target centrally.
One wide switch target on the opposite side.
One forward outlet beyond the switch target.
Add one or two recovering defenders.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder kicks towards the intended target.
The intercept player marks or wins possession.
The short release and switch target move immediately.
The interceptor may:
Kick directly to the switch.
Use the short release before switching.
The football moves to the opposite side.
The switch target delivers to the forward outlet.
Recovering defenders attempt to close the switch lanes.
Players rotate through all positions.
Repeat from both sides.
The intercept player must decide whether the direct switch is safe.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan the opposite side before completing the intercept.
Recognise where the opposition has shifted.
Use a short release when the direct switch is too difficult.
Kick with appropriate distance and trajectory.
Avoid floating the football across the ground.
coachingCues: “Win it and see the far side.”
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Accuracy of the final outlet kick.
progressions: Require a long non-preferred foot kick.
Continue into a live forward entry.
regressions: Allow the interceptor to begin with the football.
successIndicators: Choose direct or assisted switch appropriately.
matchApplication:
This drill develops the ability to exploit opposition shape after:
An intercept mark.
A turnover near the boundary.
A defensive spoil.
A pressured forward entry.
A loose-ball win at half-back.

title: Kick-In Short Option
objective: Develop the ability to execute a safe and accurate short kick from a kick-in situation. Players learn to coordinate the receiver’s lead with the kicker’s preparation and create a controlled first possession from defence.
players: Minimum: 6 Ideal: 10–18 Maximum: 24 using both sides
groundSize:
Defensive 50 or equivalent area
Approximately 40 m × 35 m
setup:
Use the goal square or create a kick-in starting area.
Place two short receiving cones:
One left.
One right.
Position each receiver approximately 15–20 metres from the kicker and five to ten metres wide of the goal square.
Place a second outlet target beyond each short receiver.
Players form lines at kicker, short receiver and outlet positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The kicker retrieves or begins with the football.
The short receiver holds position until the kicker is ready.
The receiver leads towards open space.
The kicker delivers a short, firm pass.
The receiver marks and opens towards the next outlet.
The receiver kicks to the outlet target.
Players rotate through each role.
Alternate left and right options.
The receiver should not begin the lead so early that they become stationary.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Keep the football away from imaginary central pressure.
Prepare the next disposal before the mark.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Difference between left and right execution.
Whether the same option is used repeatedly.
progressions: Add a player on the mark.
Continue into a live defensive exit.
regressions: Allow the kicker additional preparation time.
matchApplication:
Short kick-ins are used to:
Secure the first possession.
Draw the opposition forward.
Begin a switch.
Access a designated distributor.
Avoid an immediate long contest.

title: Kick-In Switch
objective: Develop the ability to use a short possession and switch the football across the defensive area after a kick-in. Players learn to draw pressure towards one side before accessing the open side.
groundSize:
Defensive 50 or equivalent area
Approximately 50 m × 45 m
setup:
Create:
Kick-in starting position.
Short receiver on one side.
Central release player.
Wide switch target on the opposite side.
Final outlet further up the ground.
Add one or two passive defenders to influence the direct side.
howTheDrillWorks:
The kicker uses the short option.
The short receiver marks and scans centrally.
The short receiver kicks to the central release.
The central release opens towards the opposite side.
The central player kicks to the wide switch target.
The switch target delivers to the final outlet.
Players follow disposals and rotate.
Repeat from both sides.
Add defender movement once the pattern is understood.
The switch target must hold width until the football is ready to transfer.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Maintain width on the opposite side.
Move the football before defenders recover.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Timing of the initial short kick.
progressions: Continue into a live transition game.
successIndicators: Exit the defensive area under control.
matchApplication:
Kick-in switches are used to:
Move the opposition across the ground.
Access the open side.
Avoid a down-the-line contest.
Create an uncontested defensive exit.
Launch transition from full-back.

title: Kick-In Play-On and Long Kick
primarySkill: Long Kick After Playing On from a Kick-In
objective: Develop the ability to play on from a kick-in, gain distance and execute a long, accurate kick to a target outside the defensive area.
players: Minimum: 6 Ideal: 10–18 Maximum: 24 using both sides
setup:
Use the goal square or create a kick-in start.
Place:
A play-on gate five to ten metres ahead.
One wide target zone.
One central target zone.
Receivers 35–50 metres away.
Adjust distance to player capability.
howTheDrillWorks:
The kicker begins inside the kick-in area.
The kicker scans both target zones.
The kicker plays on through the gate.
The kicker accelerates for several steps.
The kicker prepares the football.
The kicker delivers a long kick to the selected target zone.
The receiver marks or gathers.
Players rotate through kicker and receiver roles.
Alternate target sides.
Optional rule:
The coach calls the target zone as the kicker plays on.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Generate power through leg speed and follow-through.
Select a target within realistic range.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the player sacrifices balance for distance.
progressions: Add a player on the mark.
Add a decision between short and long options.
regressions: Allow the kicker to begin outside the square.
matchApplication:
This drill applies when a kick-in player:
Recognises space ahead.
Gains distance by playing on.
Kicks over the first defensive line.
Accesses a wide outlet.
Launches a fast defensive exit.

title: Kick-In Decision Game
objective: Develop live kick-in decisions against an organised defensive structure. Players learn to select between short possession, switching play, playing on and kicking long according to the available space.
groundSize:
Defensive half of the ground
Approximately 80 m × full or reduced width
equipment: Bibs for attacking and defending teams.
setup:
Use the defensive half of the ground.
Divide players into:
Kick-in attacking team.
Defending team.
Optional neutral players.
Place attackers in realistic positions:
Short pockets.
Central release.
Wide outlets.
High target.
Opposite-side switch.
Defenders set up in a zone or match-up structure.
howTheDrillWorks:
Every repetition begins with a kick-in.
The attacking team attempts to exit the defensive area.
The kicker may:
Use a short option.
Play on.
Switch.
Kick long.
Defenders attempt to intercept or force the football to a low-value area.
The repetition continues until:
The attacking team exits beyond the designated line.
The defence wins possession.
The football leaves the area.
Reset with another kick-in.
Rotate kickers and player roles.
Award points for successful exits and defensive turnovers.
Optional scoring:
Three points for a controlled corridor exit.
Two points for a marked wide exit.
One point for retaining possession beyond defensive 50.
Two points to defenders for an intercept and shot at goal.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
regressions: Give the kicker one free short option.
matchApplication:
This drill directly replicates kick-in situations, including:
Short possession exits.
Long contests.
Switches.
Play-on kicks.
Corridor attacks.
Defensive turnovers.

title: Kick-In Under Full Press
primarySkill: Executing Defensive Kick-Ins Against Full Press
objective: Develop the ability to exit the defensive 50 against a full opposition press. Players learn to recognise defensive structures, manipulate the press with movement, and select the safest and most effective exit option.
setup:
Set up a realistic kick-in structure.
Opposition establishes a full press.
Attacking team positions:
Short pockets.
Corridor outlet.
Wide wing.
High half-back.
Long target.
Coach restarts every repetition from a kick-in.
howTheDrillWorks:
The kicker scans the defensive setup.
Attacking players create movement to manipulate the press.
The kicker chooses the best available exit.
Play continues until:
The attacking team exits defensive 50.
The defence wins possession.
Reset and repeat using different defensive structures.
coachingPoints: Use short options to open long options.
matchApplication: Replicates kick-ins against organised AFL defensive presses.

title: Kick-In Chaos Exit
primarySkill: Decision Making in Broken Defensive Structures
objective: Train players to make effective kicking decisions when structures break down following a kick-in.
setup:
Begin with a normal kick-in.
The coach deliberately creates chaos by:
Calling random turnovers.
Sending extra defenders.
Holding players in zones.
Changing numerical advantages.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players must constantly solve changing situations while attempting to move the football cleanly from defence into attack.
Every repetition is different.
successIndicators: Players quickly recover shape after unpredictable events.
matchApplication: Replicates broken play following kick-ins, turnovers and contested exits.

title: Full Ground Exit Pattern
objective: Develop complete team kicking patterns from defensive goal square to a shot on goal.
players:
Minimum: 18
Ideal: Full Squad
Maximum: Full Squad
setup:
Use full team positions.
Begin every repetition with:
Kick-in.
Intercept mark.
Ground-ball win.
Turnover.
howTheDrillWorks:
The team must execute its complete ball movement philosophy from defence through midfield and into a quality inside-50 entry before finishing with a shot on goal.
The coach scores:
Decision quality.
Ball movement.
Structure.
Scoring opportunity.
Execution.
successIndicators: The team consistently exits defence, transitions cleanly and creates high-quality scoring opportunities.
matchApplication: Replicates complete AFL team ball movement from defensive possession to goal.

title: Banana Kick Fundamentals
objective: Develop the fundamental technique required to execute a banana kick around an obstacle or from a tight angle. Players learn the correct ball position, foot contact and body alignment before applying the skill under pressure.
setup: Create several kicking stations 20–30 metres from goal with a cone representing the player on the mark.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players begin from a stationary position.
Execute a banana kick around the cone.
Retrieve the football and rotate.
Progress to both sides of goal.
Alternate preferred and non-preferred sides.
coachingPoints: Hold the ball slightly across the body.
Contact the outside of the football.
progressions: Add a player on the mark.
matchApplication: Useful from tight angles, boundary stoppages and around the mark.

title: Banana Kick on the Run
objective: Develop the ability to execute an accurate banana kick while running at game speed.
setup: Players run onto a rolling football before executing a banana kick around a cone representing the player on the mark.
matchApplication: Replicates broken-play shots from the pocket.

title: Tight Angle Finish
objective: Develop confidence and execution when finishing from acute angles around goal.
setup: Players shoot from both forward pockets at increasing distances.
matchApplication: Replicates shots from the forward pocket.

title: Snap Kick Fundamentals
objective: Develop correct snap-kicking mechanics for shots at goal from congestion or slight angles.
setup: Players practise stationary snap kicks from multiple angles around goal.
matchApplication: Useful from congestion and set-shot angles.

title: Snap Kick Under Pressure
primarySkill: Executing a Snap Under Defensive Pressure
objective: Develop the ability to execute a successful snap kick while under immediate defensive pressure.
setup: Players receive a handball under pressure before snapping at goal.
matchApplication: Replicates front-and-square scoring opportunities.

title: Goal Square Chaos Finish
objective: Develop players' ability to score from unpredictable contests inside the goal square.
setup: The coach throws or kicks unpredictable footballs into a congested goal-square area where attackers and defenders compete.
matchApplication: Replicates real AFL goal-square chaos following spills, spoils and ground-ball contests.

title: Set Shot Routine Builder
primarySkill: Developing a Consistent Set Shot Routine
objective: Develop a repeatable pre-kick routine that remains consistent regardless of distance, angle or match pressure.
players: Minimum: 2 Ideal: 6–12 Maximum: Unlimited using multiple stations
setup:
Create set-shot stations at varying distances and angles.
Each player follows exactly the same routine before every kick.
howTheDrillWorks:
Mark the football.
Step back into the routine.
Complete breathing sequence.
Visualise the flight.
Commit to the kick.
Record routine consistency rather than only goals scored.
successIndicators: Players perform identical routines regardless of outcome.
matchApplication: Creates reliable performance under pressure.

title: Pressure Set Shot
objective: Develop the ability to maintain routine and execution while experiencing realistic match pressure.
setup: Players complete set shots while teammates create realistic crowd pressure and scoreboard scenarios.
matchApplication: Replicates game-winning set shots.

title: Fatigue Set Shot
objective: Develop technical consistency immediately after repeated high-intensity efforts.
setup: Players complete repeated sprint efforts before taking a set shot.
matchApplication: Replicates fourth-quarter set shots.

title: Goal Kicking Circuit
objective: Develop complete goal-kicking versatility by rotating through multiple finishing scenarios.
setup:
Create six stations including:
Straight set shot.
Tight angle.
Snap.
Banana.
Running shot.
Ground-ball finish.
howTheDrillWorks: Players rotate continuously through every station before recording scores.
matchApplication: Replicates every common scoring opportunity.

title: Boundary Line Banana Challenge
objective: Develop confidence executing banana kicks from progressively tighter boundary-line positions.
setup: Mark five progressively tighter kicking locations along the boundary.
matchApplication: Replicates pocket finishes.

title: Around-the-Mark Specialist
primarySkill: Scoring Around the Player on the Mark
objective: Teach players to select the highest-percentage finish based on the position of the player on the mark.
setup:
Use movable cones representing different mark positions.
Players must decide:
Drop punt.
Snap.
Banana.
before every kick.
matchApplication: Improves tactical goal kicking.

title: Goal Kicking Decision Matrix
objective:
Develop decision making using the AFL goal-kicking matrix based on:
Distance.
Angle.
Pressure.
Dominant foot.
Players must verbalise why they selected:
Drop punt.
Snap.
Banana.
before executing.
matchApplication: Builds intelligent shot selection.

title: Corridor Kick Decision
objective: Develop the ability to recognise when to attack through the corridor and when to retain possession or switch play.
setup:
Mark a central corridor approximately 15 metres wide.
Play 5 v 5 or 6 v 6 with two wide channels.
Teams score bonus points for successfully using the corridor before entering the forward zone.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins from half-back.
Teams progress the ball using kicks.
Players choose to:
Attack through the corridor.
Switch wide.
Retain possession.
If the corridor closes, players must immediately adapt.
Continue until a score or turnover.
coachingPoints: Support behind and ahead of the ball.
successIndicators: Players consistently identify high-value corridor opportunities.
matchApplication: Replicates AFL transition through the corridor.

title: Switch or Go Forward
objective: Teach players to instantly recognise whether to switch play or attack directly.
setup: The coach continually changes defensive positioning so players must determine whether the switch or direct option provides the greatest advantage.
matchApplication: Replicates AFL defensive exits and wing transition.

title: Corridor or Boundary Game
objective: Develop players' understanding of when the corridor is the highest-value option and when boundary football is the better tactical choice.
setup: Teams receive bonus points for making the correct tactical decision rather than simply scoring.
matchApplication: Improves tactical football intelligence.

title: Pressure Release Kick
primarySkill: Releasing Pressure with the Correct Kick
objective: Develop the ability to identify and execute the best release kick while under immediate defensive pressure.
setup: Attackers begin trapped inside a confined area and must escape through accurate kicking.
matchApplication: Replicates defensive pressure exits.

title: High Press Escape
objective: Develop effective kicking solutions against aggressive opposition presses.
setup:
Defenders establish an AFL-style high press.
Attackers attempt multiple exit strategies.

title: Forward Half Retention
objective: Develop controlled possession inside attacking 50 before creating a high-quality scoring opportunity.
setup: Teams maintain possession inside forward 50 before attempting a score.
matchApplication: Replicates AFL forward-half possession football.

title: Chaos Exit Decision
objective: Develop composure during unpredictable football situations.
setup:
The coach deliberately creates random turnovers, spills and unexpected numbers.
Players must continually solve the new situation.

title: Elite Disposal Chain
objective: Develop elite AFL-level disposal chains through multiple phases.
setup: Teams complete predetermined and reactive kicking chains through defensive, midfield and attacking zones.
matchApplication: Replicates AFL transition chains.

title: Tactical Kick Challenge
objective: Players must continually justify and execute the highest-percentage tactical kicking option.
setup: The coach pauses play after selected kicks and asks the player to explain their decision before continuing.
matchApplication: Develops football IQ alongside execution.

title: Advanced Match Scenario Rotation
primarySkill: Executing Kicks Across Multiple Match Scenarios
