objective: Develop complete kicking adaptability by rotating through realistic AFL match scenarios.
setup:
Players rotate through ten scenarios including:
Defensive kick-in.
Corridor attack.
Boundary exit.
Intercept transition.
Forward entry.
Tight-angle goal.
Fatigue set shot.
Last-minute attack.
High press exit.
Broken-play recovery.
successIndicators: Transition effectively between phases of play.
matchApplication: Integrates every advanced kicking concept developed in KK-101 to KK-110 into realistic AFL match scenarios.

title: Defender Distribution Decision
objective: Develop key defenders' ability to identify and execute the highest-percentage distribution option after gaining possession. Players learn to scan the field before disposal, recognise opposition structure and choose between short, medium or long kicking options.
setup:
Position a key defender with the football inside defensive 50.
Create:
Two short options.
One central outlet.
One wide switch option.
One long boundary option.
Two defenders adjust their positions before every repetition to alter the available kicking lanes.
howTheDrillWorks:
Coach signals play.
Defender scans all five options.
Defender selects the highest-percentage kick.
Ball movement continues for two additional disposals.
Reset with a different defensive structure.
successIndicators: Players consistently choose the highest-value distribution option.
matchApplication: Replicates intercept marks, defensive rebounds and kick-ins.

title: Half-Back Quarterback
objective: Develop the distributor's ability to control tempo and launch attacking chains from half-back.
setup: The designated distributor receives repeated possessions from varying angles while teammates continually adjust their positioning.
matchApplication: Replicates elite AFL rebounding defenders.

title: Wing Link Kick
objective: Develop the winger's ability to connect defence and attack using intelligent positioning and accurate kicking.
setup: Create repeated transition chains between half-back, wing and half-forward.
matchApplication: Replicates elite AFL wing play.

title: Midfielder Exit Kick
objective: Develop midfielders' ability to deliver effective first kicks immediately after winning possession.
setup: Players begin with a simulated clearance before selecting the best kicking option.
matchApplication: Replicates AFL stoppage exits.

title: Midfielder Pressure Kick
objective: Develop composure while delivering accurate kicks despite immediate physical pressure.
setup: Players receive controlled body contact before disposing.
matchApplication: Replicates contested midfield football.

title: Inside Midfield Release
objective: Develop the ability to identify and execute the release kick from heavy congestion.
setup: Small congested grid with outside support players.
matchApplication: Replicates AFL stoppage exits.

title: Outside Midfield Connection
objective: Develop outside midfielders' ability to receive, carry and distribute effectively.
setup: Continuous overlap kicking drill.
matchApplication: Replicates AFL transition running.

title: Forward Lead Delivery
objective: Develop precise delivery to leading forwards using the correct kicking weight and placement.
setup: Forwards lead from multiple starting positions while midfielders deliver.
coachingPoints: Keep the ball away from defenders.
matchApplication: Replicates inside-50 entries.

title: Forward Entry Distributor
objective: Develop half-forwards' ability to choose between shooting, centring or lowering the eyes inside forward 50.
setup: Multiple forward options are presented each repetition.
matchApplication: Replicates AFL attacking decision making.

title: Position-Specific Kicking Challenge
objective: Assess every player's ability to execute the kicking decisions required for their specific playing position.
setup:
Players rotate through five positional stations:
Key Defender
Half-Back Distributor
Wing
Midfielder
Forward
Each station contains unique decision-making challenges relevant to that position.
successIndicators: Execute the correct decision for their position.
matchApplication: This assessment integrates every position-specific kicking skill from KK-111 to KK-120 and prepares players for advanced elite match simulation drills beginning with KK-121 – Elite Decision-Making Under Pressure.

title: Elite Decision-Making Under Pressure
primarySkill: Selecting and Executing the Best Kicking Option Under Pressure
objective: Develop players’ ability to scan, assess risk and execute the highest-value kicking option while under immediate physical and time pressure.
setup:
Divide players into two teams.
Mark three vertical kicking channels:
Boundary channel.
Central channel.
Opposite-side channel.
Position one target player at the end of each channel.
Assign different point values to each target based on difficulty and tactical value.
Begin each repetition with a contested possession or coach-fed football.
howTheDrillWorks:
A player wins or receives possession under defensive pressure.
The player has a limited period to scan and dispose of the football.
Teammates create short, medium and long options.
The player selects the most appropriate kick based on:
Defensive positioning.
Available space.
Teammate movement.
Turnover risk.
Play continues for three to five disposals.
A turnover immediately changes the direction of play.
Reset after a successful target connection, score or boundary exit.
coachingPoints: Identify pressure before looking for distance.
Use the safest attacking option rather than the most ambitious option.
Keep feet active while assessing the field.
Understand the consequences of central turnovers.
Balance speed of play with disposal quality.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Support movement around the ball carrier.
progressions: Require alternating short and long options.
matchApplication: Replicates high-pressure possessions where players must make rapid kicking decisions through congestion, during transition or late in matches.

title: Scoreboard Scenario Kicking
primarySkill: Adapting Kicking Decisions to the Match Situation
objective: Develop players’ ability to alter kicking choices according to the score, time remaining and field position.
setup:
Prepare several match scenarios, including:
Leading by five points with two minutes remaining.
Trailing by four points with ninety seconds remaining.
Scores level with thirty seconds remaining.
Leading by one point from a defensive kick-in.
Trailing by ten points midway through the final quarter.
Set players into realistic field positions before each scenario begins.
howTheDrillWorks:
Coach announces the score and time remaining.
Play begins from a designated field position.
Players must adjust their kicking decisions to suit the scenario.
The coach manages the countdown.
Play continues until:
Time expires.
A score occurs.
Possession is lost.
The tactical objective is achieved.
Players briefly review the decisions made before starting the next scenario.
coachingPoints: Understand whether the team needs possession, territory or speed.
Recognise when boundary play is appropriate.
Use short kicks when controlling the clock.
Attack centrally when rapid scoring is required.
Know when to take ground and when to stop and assess.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Kicking choices relative to the scoreboard.
progressions: Do not announce the tactical solution.
Allow the opposition to select its defensive strategy.
successIndicators: Create scoring opportunities when time is limited.
matchApplication: Replicates late-game situations where kicking decisions are influenced by the score, clock and tactical requirements.

title: Final Two-Minute Possession
primarySkill: Retaining Possession to Protect a Lead
objective: Develop the team’s ability to maintain possession and deny the opposition opportunities when protecting a narrow lead late in a match.
setup:
One team begins five points ahead with two minutes remaining.
The leading team starts with possession at half-back.
The opposition establishes a full defensive press.
Mark boundary and central channels.
The leading team must retain possession until time expires.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins from a mark or free kick at half-back.
The leading team uses controlled kicking to retain possession.
Players must continually reposition after disposing of the football.
The opposition applies realistic pressure and attempts to force a turnover.
The leading team wins if it retains possession or forces a safe stoppage until time expires.
The defending team wins if it creates a scoring opportunity from a turnover.
Teams swap roles after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Create safe short options at different depths.
Avoid kicking backwards without a follow-up option.
Take time off the clock legally.
Support the receiver immediately after every kick.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players maintain depth and width.
Ability to remain composed under a full press.
Team response when the first option is denied.
progressions: Reduce the lead to one point.
Remove the ability to kick backwards twice consecutively.
successIndicators: Retain possession for the required period.
matchApplication: Replicates late-match possession control when protecting a narrow lead.

title: Final Two-Minute Attack
primarySkill: Rapid Ball Movement When Chasing a Score
objective: Develop the team’s ability to move the football rapidly and create a high-quality scoring opportunity when trailing late in a match.
setup:
The attacking team trails by four points with two minutes remaining.
Play begins from defensive 50.
The defending team sets up behind the football.
Players begin in realistic positional structures.
The attacking team must create a scoring opportunity before time expires.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team gains possession in defence.
Players must quickly decide whether to:
Attack through the corridor.
Use the wing and overlap.
Switch before accelerating.
Kick long to an isolated contest.
The countdown continues throughout the repetition.
The attacking team wins by scoring a goal.
The defending team wins by forcing a turnover, boundary stoppage or time expiry.
Teams rotate roles.
coachingPoints: Avoid repeated sideways possession when time is limited.
Create multiple scoring options rather than relying on one target.
progressions: Allow the defending team to flood deeper.
successIndicators: Move the ball quickly from defence.
Maintain support around the ball carrier.
matchApplication: Replicates late-game attacking situations where the team must score quickly from the back half.

title: Boundary-Line Exit Under Pressure
objective: Develop the ability to move the football safely and effectively along the boundary when central options are unavailable.
setup:
Mark a narrow channel along one boundary.
Position attackers and defenders throughout the channel.
Place a target zone at the far end.
Begin each repetition with possession deep in defence.
Restrict central access during the first phase.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with a mark near the boundary.
Players must create options ahead, behind and inside.
The team progresses the football primarily through kicks.
The boundary may be used as protection but players must avoid becoming trapped.
The team scores by reaching the target zone under control.
Defenders score by forcing a turnover or stoppage.
Play resets after each outcome.
coachingPoints: Kick to the receiver’s safe side.
Avoid leading every player into the same space.
Prepare for a boundary stoppage if possession cannot be retained.
Transition immediately if the football is turned over.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Placement of kicks relative to the boundary.
progressions: Add a central bonus gate that may open unexpectedly.
Require a mark before entering the target zone.
successIndicators: Place kicks to the safe side.
matchApplication: Replicates boundary-side exits when the opposition has closed the corridor.

title: Corridor Re-Entry Kick
primarySkill: Re-Entering the Corridor After Boundary Possession
objective: Develop the ability to recognise and execute the correct moment to move the football from the boundary back into the corridor.
setup:
Mark a boundary channel and a central corridor.
Begin possession in the boundary channel.
Position central attackers and defenders in the corridor.
Create two central entry gates.
The coach may open or close gates using coloured signals.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team moves the football along the boundary.
Central players continually reposition to create an entry lane.
The ball carrier scans for the corridor option.
When the corridor becomes available, the player executes the re-entry kick.
The team accelerates forward following the central connection.
If the corridor remains closed, the team retains possession or continues along the boundary.
A turnover immediately reverses the direction of play.
coachingPoints: Avoid entering the corridor without forward support.
Wait until the central receiver has separation.
Move quickly after the central kick.
Maintain width until the corridor opportunity appears.
Recognise whether the defence is shifting or stationary.
Avoid telegraphing the kick too early.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Speed of transition after the kick.
progressions: Reduce the width of the corridor.
Require a forward-50 entry after corridor connection.
Allow defenders to change structure during play.
successIndicators: Recognise the correct corridor entry moment.
Maintain structure before and after the kick.
matchApplication: Replicates switching from controlled boundary play into aggressive corridor transition.

title: Defensive Switch Intercept Risk
primarySkill: Executing Defensive Switches Without Exposing Intercept Opportunities
objective: Develop players’ understanding of when a defensive switch is available and how to execute it without creating a dangerous central turnover.
setup:
Position the attacking team across defensive 50.
Place pressing forwards between the ball and the opposite side.
Create short, medium and long switch options.
Mark a central turnover zone where defensive interceptions receive bonus points.
Begin with a mark near one boundary.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier assesses whether the switch is available.
Teammates move to create safe angles and depth.
The team may:
Complete the switch.
Retain possession.
Exit down the original side.
Defenders attempt to anticipate and intercept the switch.
The attacking team scores by reaching the opposite wing under control.
The defending team receives extra points for intercepting centrally.
Reset after the outcome.
coachingPoints: Ensure the switch receiver has separation.
Use sufficient depth behind the football.
Communicate whether the switch is safe.
Keep an exit option on the original side.
Understand that not every switch should be completed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players retain the original-side option.
successIndicators: Identify whether the switch is genuinely available.
matchApplication: Replicates defensive switches against organised forward-half pressure.

title: Switch Completion to Forward Entry
primarySkill: Converting a Defensive Switch into an Attacking Forward Entry
objective: Develop the team’s ability to complete a defensive switch, accelerate through the open side and finish with a high-quality forward-50 entry.
setup:
Position players in defensive, midfield and attacking zones.
Begin with possession near one defensive boundary.
Set defenders to protect the initial side.
Leave the opposite wing partially open.
Position forwards to begin moving only after the switch is initiated.
howTheDrillWorks:
The defending team initiates a switch across defensive 50.
Once the opposite-side receiver marks the football, the team accelerates.
Wing and midfield players provide forward-running options.
The ball must move through at least one midfield connection.
The team completes the sequence with an inside-50 kick.
Forwards attempt to mark or create a scoring opportunity.
A turnover results in immediate defensive transition.
Reset from the opposite side.
coachingPoints: Complete the switch with speed and accuracy.
Accelerate once the open side is accessed.
Avoid slowing the play after gaining advantage.
Deliver inside 50 to space rather than directly at defenders.
Maintain defensive balance behind the ball.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the team attacks immediately after shifting the defence.
progressions: Set a maximum time to enter forward 50.
Require a goal to complete the repetition.
Allow defenders to block the preferred switch side.
regressions: Reduce the number of midfield connections.
matchApplication: Replicates full-ground transition after successfully shifting an opposition defensive press.

title: Turnover Punishment Kick Chain
primarySkill: Attacking Immediately After an Opposition Turnover
objective: Develop the ability to recognise and exploit opposition disorganisation immediately after winning possession from a turnover.
setup:
Create two teams in realistic field positions.
The coach begins with controlled possession by one team.
At a random moment, the coach creates a turnover through:
A misplaced kick.
A loose football.
An intercept opportunity.
A whistle and possession reversal.
Place scoring targets at the attacking end.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team begins in possession.
The coach creates an unexpected turnover.
The new attacking team must immediately spread and attack.
The first player in possession assesses:
Corridor.
Wide outlet.
Forward isolation.
Short retention option.
The team attempts to complete a scoring chain before the opposition resets.
If the opposition regains possession, direction reverses again.
Reset after a score or defensive recovery.
coachingPoints: Scan forward immediately after winning possession.
Recognise when the opposition is out of shape.
Move the football before the defence recovers.
Avoid attacking blindly when no advantage exists.
Lower the eyes before entering forward 50.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: First kicking decision after the turnover.
Defensive reaction from the team that lost possession.
Whether players recognise when to slow down.
progressions: Require the first disposal to be a kick.
Begin from different areas of the ground.
Allow repeated turnovers within the same play.
regressions: Announce the turnover before it occurs.
successIndicators: Recognise when the transition advantage has ended.
matchApplication: Replicates scoring chains created from intercept marks, pressure turnovers and loose-ball recoveries.

title: Turnover Recovery Kick
primarySkill: Regaining Controlled Possession After Losing the Football
objective: Develop the team’s ability to respond after a kicking turnover, regain possession and execute a controlled recovery kick rather than immediately turning the football over again.
setup:
Divide players into two teams.
Mark two recovery target gates on opposite sides of the area.
Begin with one team moving the football by foot.
The coach calls or creates a turnover.
The team that lost possession must apply immediate pressure and attempt to regain the football.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins a kicking chain.
A turnover occurs naturally or is created by the coach.
The team that lost possession applies immediate pressure.
If possession is regained, the player must execute a controlled recovery kick through one of the target gates.
The recovery kick cannot be a blind clearance unless no possession option exists.
The opposition attempts to force a second turnover.
Teams receive points for:
Regaining possession.
Completing the recovery kick.
Preventing a score.
Reset after the sequence is completed.
coachingPoints: Stay composed when possession is regained.
Look for a safe outlet before clearing.
Use the boundary if the team remains under pressure.
Rebuild offensive shape after the recovery kick.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Pressure applied to the new ball carrier.
Selection and execution of the recovery kick.
progressions: Add a time limit for the recovery kick.
Require the recovery chain to continue into attack.
regressions: Allow additional time after the regain.
Increase the size of target gates.
matchApplication: Replicates the critical moments following a kicking error when teams must defend, regain control and reconnect with a safe disposal.

title: Defensive Scramble Release Kick
primarySkill: Executing a Controlled Release Kick from Defensive Scramble
objective: Develop players’ ability to regain possession in a disorganised defensive situation and execute a controlled release kick rather than a blind clearance into further pressure.
setup:
Position attackers and defenders inside defensive 50.
Create two wide release gates and one central release gate outside the area.
The coach begins each repetition with an unpredictable high ball, ground ball or deflection.
Defenders begin slightly out of position to create a realistic scramble.
Attackers attempt to win possession and score.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach introduces an unpredictable football into defensive 50.
Defenders compete to spoil, gather or intercept.
Once possession is secured, the defending team must identify a release option.
The first kick should connect with a teammate or travel safely through a release gate.
Attackers apply immediate pressure and attempt to force a turnover.
The defending team scores for exiting under control.
Attackers score by winning possession and kicking a goal.
Reset with players in different starting positions.
coachingPoints: Secure possession before attempting the release.
Scan outside the contest before gathering.
Protect the corridor during the scramble.
Use the boundary when central options are unsafe.
Avoid kicking directly back into congestion.
Rebuild team structure after the exit.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Direction and placement of the release kick.
Reactions if the first release option is denied.
progressions: Reduce the size of the defensive area.
Require the exit to continue into a forward entry.
successIndicators: Win or secure the defensive football.
Re-establish team structure after the scramble.
matchApplication: Replicates defensive ground-ball contests, spoils and loose-ball situations where a composed exit kick can prevent repeat opposition entries.

title: Repeat Entry Defensive Exit
primarySkill: Exiting Defensive 50 After Repeated Opposition Entries
objective: Develop the ability to withstand repeated forward entries, regain control and execute a composed defensive exit while players are fatigued and structurally disrupted.
setup:
Position one team inside defensive 50.
Place attacking players across the forward half.
Keep several footballs with coaches positioned outside the area.
Mark an exit line approximately 20 metres beyond defensive 50.
Defenders must successfully exit the football to end the repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach delivers the first football into attacking 50.
Attackers attempt to score.
If defenders spoil, intercept or win possession but fail to exit, the coach introduces another football.
The sequence continues until:
The defending team completes a controlled exit beyond the exit line.
The attacking team scores a goal.
A predetermined number of entries is completed.
Defenders must maintain communication and structure despite fatigue.
Teams rotate after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Defend the most dangerous space first.
Spread immediately when possession is won.
Avoid rushing the first exit kick.
Use short possession to create a safer long exit.
Recognise when territory is more valuable than retention.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Speed of spread after possession is won.
Quality of the first exit decision.
Whether players repeat the same unsuccessful exit.
Work rate after a failed clearance.
progressions: Increase the number of repeat entries.
Require two completed kicks before the exit counts.
regressions: Allow defenders a free kick after an intercept mark.
Limit the number of repeat entries.
Use controlled rather than full pressure.
successIndicators: Maintain defensive structure through repeated phases.
matchApplication: Replicates sustained opposition pressure when a team must absorb repeated inside-50 entries before successfully rebounding.

title: Long Down-the-Line Contest Kick
primarySkill: Executing a Long Kick to a Boundary-Side Contest
objective: Develop the ability to execute a long down-the-line kick that gives teammates the best chance to mark, force a stoppage or bring the football safely to ground.
setup:
Mark a boundary channel.
Position a kicker approximately 45–60 metres from a target contest.
Place one target player and one defender at the contest.
Position two ground-level support players around the drop zone.
Mark a safe landing zone between the target and the boundary.
howTheDrillWorks:
The kicker receives the football under controlled pressure.
The target player leads or holds position down the line.
The kicker delivers a long kick into the safe landing zone.
The target attempts to mark or bring the football to ground safely.
Ground-level players compete for the crumb.
The attacking team scores for:
A mark.
A boundary stoppage.
Controlled possession from the contest.
The defending team scores for an uncontested intercept or clean rebound.
Rotate roles regularly.
coachingPoints: Kick to the boundary side of the target.
Give the target sufficient height and time when required.
Avoid placing the football inside where defenders can counterattack.
Match trajectory to the target’s positioning.
Ensure ground-level support arrives at the drop zone.
Maintain defensive coverage behind the kick.
Understand when a contest kick is tactically appropriate.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Kick placement relative to the target.
Outcome when the mark is not taken.
progressions: Introduce live pressure on the kicker.
Allow the contest to continue into transition.
regressions: Allow the kicker additional preparation time.
successIndicators: Place the football on the safe side.
Give the target a genuine opportunity to compete.
Achieve a mark, stoppage or controlled ground-ball win.
matchApplication: Replicates long boundary exits and territory kicks when short possession or corridor options are unavailable.

title: Contest Kick Ground-Level Setup
primarySkill: Supporting a Long Contest Kick at Ground Level
objective: Develop coordinated positioning around a long kicking contest so the team is prepared to win the spill, force a stoppage or defend an opposition possession.
setup:
Create a long-kick starting point and a marked contest zone.
Position one aerial target and one direct opponent inside the zone.
Place attacking support players at:
Front of the contest.
Boundary side.
Defensive side.
Place matching defenders around the area.
Begin each repetition with a long kick into the contest.
howTheDrillWorks:
The kicker delivers to the aerial contest.
The target attempts to mark or direct the football to a designated area.
Ground-level players hold their roles until the ball’s flight is clear.
Players compete for the spill.
The team winning possession must complete a kick through a target gate.
If the football leaves the area, reset and rotate positions.
coachingPoints: Avoid all players moving directly underneath the football.
Cover front, boundary and defensive-side positions.
Read the likely direction of the spoil.
Maintain balance between attack and defence.
Use the first possession cleanly after the contest.
React immediately if the opposition wins the ball.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Defensive reaction when possession is lost.
progressions: Add more players around the contest.
Continue play into a scoring zone.
regressions: Allow the coach to position players before each contest.
successIndicators: Avoid overcommitting to the aerial contest.
Complete a controlled disposal after possession.
matchApplication: Replicates team structure around long boundary kicks, stoppage exits and contested forward entries.

title: Outnumbered Contest Kick
primarySkill: Managing a Necessary Kick to an Outnumbered Contest
objective: Develop players’ ability to minimise turnover damage when a kick to an outnumbered contest is unavoidable.
setup:
Position one attacking target against two defenders.
Place the contest near a boundary.
Position one or two attacking ground-level support players outside the contest.
The kicker begins under pressure with no uncontested short option.
Mark a safe territory zone beyond the contest.
howTheDrillWorks:
The kicker scans for alternatives before deciding to kick long.
When the contest kick is required, the kicker places the football towards the boundary side.
The attacking target competes to:
Mark.
Force the football out.
Bring it to a predictable ground-level area.
Support players attempt to win the spill or force a stoppage.
Defenders attempt to intercept and rebound.
Points are awarded based on the outcome:
Mark by the target.
Boundary stoppage.
Attacking ground-ball win.
Defensive intercept and rebound.
Rotate all roles.
coachingPoints: Confirm that no safer option exists.
Kick away from the most dangerous opposition space.
Give the target sufficient time to compete.
Avoid kicking short of the contest.
Position support players for the likely spill.
Prepare defensively if the opposition intercepts.
progressions: Introduce a second attacking support player.
Allow full live transition after the contest.
regressions: Use one defender instead of two.
Allow the target to begin in front position.
Use passive pressure on the kicker.
successIndicators: Recognise when the contest kick is necessary.
Place the football in a low-risk area.
Force stoppages or win ground-level possession.
Maintain defensive balance behind the kick.
matchApplication: Replicates situations where pressure and field position require a territory kick despite an opposition numerical advantage.

title: Numerical Advantage Recognition Kick
primarySkill: Identifying and Kicking to a Numerical Advantage
objective: Develop players’ ability to quickly recognise numerical advantages around the ground and deliver the football to the area where their team has superior numbers.
setup:
Mark three target zones across the ground.
Position different numbers of attackers and defenders in each zone.
Change the numerical balance before every repetition.
Place a ball carrier approximately 30–45 metres from the zones.
Add one pressure defender near the kicker.
howTheDrillWorks:
The kicker scans all three zones.
Players inside the zones move to create separation.
The kicker identifies where the attacking team has:
A clear numerical advantage.
The strongest positional advantage.
The safest next-possession opportunity.
The kicker delivers to the selected zone.
Players compete and attempt to complete a follow-up kick.
The coach changes numbers and positioning before the next repetition.
Rotate kickers and zone players.
coachingPoints: Distinguish between numerical and positional advantage.
Avoid kicking to a crowded zone simply because it is closer.
Weight the kick to allow teammates to use their numbers.
Reassess if defenders move during preparation.
Follow the kick to support the next possession.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Ability to adjust when the advantage changes.
progressions: Conceal player numbers until the kicker turns to receive.
regressions: Pause before each repetition for guided scanning.
matchApplication: Replicates the scanning and tactical awareness required to exploit spare players during transition, switches and forward entries.

title: Spare Player Elimination Kick
primarySkill: Kicking Around or Through an Opposition Spare Player
objective: Develop the ability to identify an opposition spare player and use intelligent kicking, movement and field position to reduce that player’s influence.
equipment: Coloured vest for the spare defender
setup:
Position one team in possession across half-back and midfield.
Place forwards in attacking positions.
Nominate one defender as the spare player.
The spare may position behind the ball or in front of the key forward.
Mark wide, central and short-entry zones.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with possession outside forward 50.
Players identify the spare defender’s location.
The team attempts to move the spare through:
Switching play.
Short possession.
Changing angles.
Using a player behind the ball.
Once the spare is displaced, the team enters forward 50.
The spare defender attempts to intercept and launch a rebound.
The attacking team scores for creating a mark or controlled possession inside 50.
The defending team scores for an intercept and successful exit.
coachingPoints: Identify the spare before entering forward 50.
Avoid repeatedly kicking directly to the spare.
Use possession to move the defender laterally.
Create a short option in front of the defensive block.
Use forwards to occupy and manipulate defenders.
Maintain defensive balance in case of turnover.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Quality of switches and short connections.
Forward movement designed to occupy defenders.
progressions: Allow the spare to change positions during play.
Require a score to complete the repetition.
regressions: Restrict the spare to one zone.
Pause play to identify the spare.
matchApplication: Replicates attacking against an opposition loose defender positioned behind the ball or in front of a key forward.

title: Defensive Zone Penetration Kick
objective: Develop the ability to identify and execute kicks that penetrate an organised defensive zone without exposing the team to high-risk turnovers.
setup:
Divide the ground into defensive, midfield and attacking zones.
Position the defending team in an organised zone structure.
The attacking team begins with controlled possession in the defensive half.
Mark bonus gates between defenders in the midfield and forward lines.
The attacking team must penetrate the zone primarily through kicking.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team circulates possession to move the zone.
Players ahead of the football adjust their positioning to create passing lanes.
The ball carrier identifies whether to:
Kick through the zone.
Kick around the zone.
Retain possession.
Take territory to a contest.
Bonus points are awarded for penetrating through a gate and retaining possession.
The defending team attempts to intercept and counterattack.
Play continues until a score, turnover or successful exit.
Teams rotate roles.
coachingPoints: Move the zone before attempting penetration.
Scan through the defensive line rather than only around it.
Avoid slow, floating passes through central space.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Movement of players between defensive lines.
Timing and trajectory of penetrating kicks.
Ability to recognise when penetration is unsafe.
regressions: Walk through the defensive structure before live play.
successIndicators: Move the defensive zone before attacking it.
matchApplication: Replicates controlled ball movement against teams defending with organised zones, presses or layered structures.

title: Defensive Line-Breaking Kick
primarySkill: Breaking a Defensive Line with an Aggressive Kick
objective: Develop players’ ability to identify and execute a high-value kick that breaks an opposition defensive line and creates immediate attacking momentum.
setup:
Mark three horizontal defensive lines across the area.
Position defenders along each line.
Place attacking receivers in spaces between and beyond the lines.
Begin with possession behind the first defensive line.
Mark bonus zones beyond each line.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with controlled possession.
Players move to create a passing lane through or over a defensive line.
The ball carrier assesses whether a line-breaking kick is available.
A successful kick must:
Bypass at least one defensive line.
Connect with a teammate.
Allow the team to retain attacking momentum.
The receiver plays on or quickly moves the football forward.
The defending team attempts to intercept and counterattack.
Play continues until the final target zone is reached or possession changes.
coachingPoints: Use the correct trajectory for the available lane.
Avoid forcing line-breaking kicks into organised numbers.
Run forward immediately after the kick.
Provide support on both sides of the receiver.
Recognise when a safer possession kick is required.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Forward support after the line break.
Team reaction when the kick is unavailable.
progressions: Add pressure to the ball carrier.
Reduce the width of passing lanes.
Continue into a full-ground scoring sequence.
successIndicators: Execute kicks with appropriate speed and accuracy.
matchApplication: Replicates aggressive kicks that bypass opposition defensive layers and launch rapid attacking transition.

title: Advanced Kicking Scenario Assessment
primarySkill: Applying Advanced Kicking Decisions Across Match Scenarios
objective: Assess players’ ability to apply advanced kicking skills across a range of realistic match scenarios involving defensive exits, numerical advantages, contested kicking, zone penetration and turnover management.
setup:
Create ten advanced kicking scenarios across the ground:
Defensive scramble release.
Repeat-entry exit.
Long boundary contest kick.
Ground-level contest setup.
Outnumbered contest management.
Numerical advantage recognition.
Opposition spare-player manipulation.
Defensive-zone penetration.
Defensive line-breaking kick.
Turnover recovery and transition.
Players rotate through positional and decision-making roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins each scenario from a realistic match position.
Players receive limited information before play begins.
The team must identify the tactical problem and execute an appropriate kicking solution.
Each scenario continues until:
The tactical objective is achieved.
A score occurs.
Possession changes.
The allotted time expires.
Coaches assess:
Decision quality.
Kicking execution.
Communication.
Team structure.
Transition after the disposal.
Players rotate through different roles and field positions.
Scores are recorded to create individual and team kicking profiles.
coachingPoints: Understand field position and turnover consequences.
Match the kick type to the tactical problem.
Maintain support ahead of and behind the football.
Adjust immediately when the preferred option closes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Understanding of numerical and positional advantage.
progressions: Allow opposition coaches to adjust defensive structures.
Add fatigue efforts before each scenario.
Run all scenarios within one continuous match simulation.
successIndicators: Maintain team structure around the football.
Apply advanced kicking principles across multiple field positions.
matchApplication: Provides a comprehensive assessment of advanced kicking decisions required during defensive exits, contested ball movement, transition, forward entry and late-game situations.

title: Elite Full-Ground Kicking Simulation
primarySkill: Executing Team Kicking Strategy Across the Full Ground
objective: Develop the team’s ability to execute its complete kicking system from defensive possession through midfield and into attack against realistic opposition pressure.
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Establish realistic positional structures.
Mark defensive, midfield and attacking zones.
Begin repetitions from:
Kick-ins.
Intercept marks.
Centre clearances.
Boundary stoppages.
Opposition turnovers.
Assign each team a specific kicking strategy.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins from a nominated match situation.
The team in possession must move the football primarily by foot.
Players may use:
Short possession.
Defensive switches.
Boundary exits.
Corridor attacks.
Long contest kicks.
The team attempts to create a controlled inside-50 entry and scoring opportunity.
Turnovers result in immediate live transition.
Coaches score decision quality, execution and team structure.
Reset after a score, stoppage or tactical objective is achieved.
coachingPoints: Support ahead of and behind the football.
Recognise when to accelerate or retain possession.
Lower the eyes before entering forward 50.
progressions: Give the opposition an extra defender.
Require specific exit or entry patterns.
matchApplication: Replicates complete AFL match ball movement and kicking decision making across all areas of the ground.

title: Opposition Press Adaptation
primarySkill: Adapting Kicking Strategy to Different Defensive Presses
objective: Develop players’ ability to recognise different opposition defensive presses and adjust their kicking strategy without requiring direct instruction from the coach.
setup:
Prepare several defensive structures:
Full-ground press.
Half-ground press.
Boundary trap.
Corridor block.
Man-on-man defence.
Loose defender behind the ball.
The defending team changes its structure before or during each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with possession in defence.
The opposition establishes one of the nominated presses.
The attacking team must identify the structure without coach assistance.
Players select an appropriate exit strategy.
Play continues until the attacking team:
Reaches the wing.
Exits the defensive half.
Creates a forward entry.
A turnover allows the defending team to attack.
The defensive structure changes for the next repetition.
coachingPoints: Identify where the opposition has placed extra numbers.
Recognise which areas have been deliberately left open.
Avoid using the same exit pattern repeatedly.
Use short kicks to open long options.
Change tempo when the opposition adjusts.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Execution after the press is beaten.
Reaction when the first option closes.
progressions: Change the defensive structure during the possession chain.
Prevent coaches from announcing the press.
Let the defending team design its own press.
regressions: Walk through each press before live play.
successIndicators: Adjust when the defensive structure changes.
matchApplication: Replicates preparing for and responding to different opposition defensive systems.

title: Weather-Condition Kicking
primarySkill: Adapting Kicking Technique to Weather Conditions
objective: Develop players’ ability to adjust kicking technique, kick selection and team strategy according to wind, rain and difficult ground conditions.
equipment: Water bottles or damp footballs where appropriate
setup:
Create stations or scenarios representing:
Kicking with the wind.
Kicking into the wind.
Crosswind kicking.
Wet-football possession.
Slippery ground-ball recovery.
Long territory kicking.
Short controlled possession.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players rotate through each weather-based scenario.
At every station, the kicker must adjust:
Ball drop.
Kick trajectory.
Power.
Target position.
Team-based phases require players to decide whether to:
Retain possession.
Take territory.
Use the boundary.
Attack centrally.
Coaches record decision quality and execution.
Finish with a live conditions-based game.
coachingPoints: Lower kick trajectory into the wind.
Avoid excessive ball height in strong crosswinds.
Keep the ball drop compact in wet conditions.
Kick to the safe side of teammates.
Value territory when clean possession is difficult.
Communicate wind direction and ball behaviour.
progressions: Use live weather conditions where safe.
Restrict kicking options according to conditions.
regressions: Explain the required adjustment before each kick.
successIndicators: Maintain effective ball movement in difficult weather.
matchApplication: Replicates the technical and tactical adjustments required during wet, windy or otherwise difficult AFL matches.

title: Wet-Weather Ball Movement
primarySkill: Executing Effective Kicks with a Wet Football
objective: Develop the technical execution and tactical decision making required to move the football effectively in wet and slippery conditions.
setup:
Dampen the footballs safely.
Mark boundary-side and central target zones.
Position players in small teams.
Begin repetitions from:
Ground balls.
Contested marks.
Loose-ball recoveries.
Defensive exits.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach introduces a wet football into a contested or loose-ball situation.
The team winning possession must decide whether to:
Complete a short kick.
Take territory.
Kick to a boundary-side contest.
Force a stoppage.
Play continues for three to six disposals.
Teams score for controlled exits, territory gains and safe stoppages.
Dangerous central turnovers are heavily penalised.
Reset and rotate starting positions.
coachingPoints: Keep two hands on the football.
Shorten the final stride where necessary.
Direct long kicks towards safe territory.
Prepare for the ball to spill from marking contests.
Accept stoppages when clean possession is unavailable.
matchApplication: Replicates wet-weather football where clean disposal, territory and contest structure become critical.

title: Wind Management Kicking
objective: Develop players’ ability to adjust kicking technique and tactical choices when kicking with, against or across strong wind.
contact: 0 – No Contact initially; controlled pressure in progression
setup:
Create four stations:
Kicking with the wind.
Kicking into the wind.
Kicking across a left-to-right wind.
Kicking across a right-to-left wind.
Include short, medium, long and goal-kicking targets.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players identify the wind direction before every kick.
The kicker announces the intended:
Starting line.
Trajectory.
Landing point.
Players execute the kick and assess the result.
Receivers adjust their positioning according to the flight.
Players rotate through all stations.
Finish with a live kicking-possession game using the wind.
coachingPoints: Drive the football lower into the wind.
Avoid allowing the ball to stall.
Control power when kicking with the wind.
Aim into crosswinds rather than directly at the final target.
Position receivers on the expected landing side.
Use the wind tactically for territory.
progressions: Require both preferred and non-preferred foot kicking.
regressions: Allow practice kicks before scoring begins.
successIndicators: Use the wind to tactical advantage.
matchApplication: Replicates the technical and strategic demands of AFL matches played in strong or changing wind.

title: Fatigue Decision-Making Game
primarySkill: Maintaining Kicking Decisions and Execution Under Fatigue
objective: Develop players’ ability to preserve kicking accuracy, tactical awareness and decision quality during repeated high-intensity efforts.
setup:
Divide players into two teams.
Mark three kicking zones and several sprint stations.
Before entering each possession phase, selected players complete a high-intensity running effort.
Create short, central, wide and long kicking options.
Position defenders to apply immediate pressure.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players complete a prescribed sprint effort.
The coach immediately introduces the football.
The team in possession must complete a kicking chain.
The ball carrier chooses between multiple options.
A turnover reverses direction.
After each phase, different players complete the fatigue effort.
The drill continues in repeated high-intensity blocks.
Coaches compare early and late decision quality.
coachingPoints: Recover breathing before disposal where time permits.
Avoid automatically kicking long when fatigued.
Communicate more clearly as fatigue increases.
Use teammates to reduce unnecessary physical load.
Preserve team shape late in the drill.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Technical consistency late in the drill.
progressions: Require full-ground transition after each possession.
matchApplication: Replicates late-quarter and late-match kicking decisions when physical fatigue affects technical execution and tactical awareness.

title: Communication-Led Kicking
primarySkill: Using Communication to Improve Kicking Decisions
objective: Develop clear, early and specific communication that helps the ball carrier identify pressure, space and the highest-value kicking option.
setup:
Divide players into attacking and defending teams.
Mark wide, central and deep target gates.
Nominate on-field communication leaders.
Begin play with the ball carrier facing away from the main playing area.
Teammates must communicate information before the player turns.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier receives possession under pressure.
Teammates communicate:
Pressure location.
Available space.
Preferred kick.
Time available.
The ball carrier turns, scans and selects an option.
The possession chain continues for four to six disposals.
Points are awarded for:
Early communication.
Correct information.
Successful execution.
Turnovers reverse direction.
Rotate communication leaders.
coachingPoints: Use specific information rather than general noise.
Call the safe side of the receiver.
Confirm whether the player has time.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Leadership when the drill becomes chaotic.
progressions: Score communication quality separately from execution.
regressions: Allow the coach to demonstrate calls.
matchApplication: Replicates the communication required to support players whose vision is limited by pressure, body position or congestion.

title: Scoreboard and Numerical Constraint Game
primarySkill: Adapting Kicking Strategy to Scoreboard and Player-Number Constraints
objective: Develop players’ ability to adjust kicking decisions when the team is leading, trailing, numerically advantaged or numerically disadvantaged.
setup:
Prepare scenarios including:
Leading by six points with one player fewer.
Trailing by ten points with one extra player.
Scores level with two minutes remaining.
Protecting a lead after a player leaves the ground.
Chasing a goal against a spare defender.
Retaining possession with a numerical advantage.
howTheDrillWorks:
Coach announces the score, time and player-number situation.
Teams organise their structure.
Play begins from a nominated field position.
The team in possession adapts its kicking strategy.
The opposition attempts to exploit the numerical situation.
The scenario continues until:
Time expires.
A score occurs.
The tactical objective is achieved.
Coaches briefly assess decisions before changing the scenario.
coachingPoints: Understand whether possession, territory or speed is required.
Use extra players to create uncontested kicking options.
Avoid exposing central space when outnumbered.
Change tempo according to the scoreboard.
Recognise when a stoppage is valuable.
Maintain composure during unexpected numerical changes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Kicking risk relative to the scenario.
progressions: Allow teams to design their own strategy.
regressions: Coach the preferred option during play.
matchApplication: Replicates AFL matches affected by injuries, send-offs, rotations, late-game scores and temporary numerical imbalances.

title: Elite Kicking Match Simulation
primarySkill: Applying the Complete Team Kicking System in Match Conditions
objective: Integrate all technical, tactical and position-specific kicking skills into a continuous match simulation with realistic pressure, scoring and coaching assessment.
setup:
Divide players into two match-balanced teams.
Use full positional structures.
Assign each team:
A defensive exit strategy.
A midfield transition strategy.
A forward-entry strategy.
A turnover-response strategy.
Set realistic match rules, interchange and scoring.
Prepare scenario cards that can be introduced during play.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins as a normal match simulation.
Coaches allow continuous play with minimal interruption.
Teams must apply their full kicking strategy.
At selected moments, the coach introduces scenarios such as:
Full opposition press.
Strong wind.
Wet football.
Final-two-minute situation.
Numerical disadvantage.
Spare defender.
Coaches assess both the decision and execution of each critical kick.
Teams review performance between blocks.
Play resumes with adjusted tactical objectives.
coachingPoints: Apply all kicking principles without relying on coach direction.
Protect the football in dangerous field positions.
Adapt to changing conditions and scenarios.
progressions: Require teams to self-review between blocks.
successIndicators: Make appropriate decisions across the full ground.
Communicate and organise without coach direction.
matchApplication: Provides the closest training replication of competitive AFL kicking demands before formal match play.

title: Complete Kicking Competency Assessment
primarySkill: Comprehensive Assessment of AFL Kicking Competency
objective: Provide a complete assessment of each player’s kicking technique, versatility, decision making and tactical execution across every major AFL kicking situation.
groundSize: Full Ground with Multiple Assessment Stations
setup:
Create ten assessment stations:
Basic drop-punt technique.
Short-kick accuracy.
Medium and long kicking.
Preferred and non-preferred foot.
Kicking on the run.
Kicking under pressure.
Goal kicking.
Defensive exit decisions.
Forward-entry decisions.
Full-ground match simulation.
Prepare age-appropriate scoring standards for each station.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players complete each technical station.
Coaches record:
Accuracy.
Distance.
Trajectory.
Ball-drop consistency.
Balance.
Preferred and non-preferred-side performance.
Players then complete decision-making stations under pressure.
Goal-kicking performance is assessed from:
Set shots.
Running shots.
Snaps.
Bananas.
Tight angles.
Fatigue.
Players finish with a live match simulation.
Coaches combine all results into an individual kicking profile.
Each player receives priority development areas and recommended drills.
coachingPoints: Select the correct kick for the situation.
Maintain execution under pressure and fatigue.
Use both sides of the body.
Transfer isolated skills into match play.
progressions: Compare results across multiple testing periods.
Use opposition pressure at every station.
Add match statistics to the assessment profile.
regressions: Assess one skill group per session.
Use larger targets for younger players.
successIndicators: Accurate short, medium and long disposal.
matchApplication: Provides a complete evidence-based profile of each player’s ability to execute AFL kicking skills in technical, tactical and match-pressure environments.
